records.title: Vice President Quality Control
records.description:
Shape the future of quality and patient trust. Join us as the Vice President, Global Quality Control and lead a world-class laboratory network that powers our clinical and commercial programs across the globe. Reporting to the Chief Quality Officer, you will set the enterprise strategy and build a unified, high-performing Quality Control organization that delivers reliable data, inspection-ready laboratories, and timely product release support—while advancing standardization, digital innovation, scientific excellence, and operational performance.
 
 
**Company Overview**
The work we do at FUJIFILM Biotechnologies has never been more important—and we are looking for talented candidates to join us. We are growing our locations, our capabilities, and our teams, and looking for passionate, mission-driven people like you who want to make a real difference in people’s lives.
 
 
Join FUJIFILM Biotechnologies and help make the next vaccine, cure, or gene therapy in partnership with some of the most innovative biopharma companies across the globe. We are proud to cultivate a culture that will fuel your passion, energy, and drive - what we call Genki.
 
 
Fujifilm is globally headquartered in Tokyo with over 70,000 employees across four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging. We are guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles.” Visit: https://www.fujifilm.com/us/en/about/region/careers
 
 
**Job Description**
Your impact In this enterprise role, your leadership will directly influence patient safety, product quality, inspection outcomes, batch disposition timelines, and continuity of supply across a diverse global portfolio. You will advise senior executives on investment, capacity, technology, organizational design, and regulatory strategy—shaping multi‑year business and quality plans. Your decisions will strengthen client trust, accelerate revenue recognition, reduce the cost of quality, and protect the company’s license to operate.
 
 
What you will do
 
 

* Define and execute a global Quality Control strategy, operating model, and multi‑year roadmap across sites, modalities, and development phases. Establish enterprise standards, clear decision rights, and governance forums that enable consistent, phase‑appropriate control while allowing justified site or platform differences.
* Provide executive oversight of end‑to‑end Quality Control operations, including analytical, biochemical, biological, microbiological, raw‑material, in‑process, release, and stability testing; as well as environmental and utility monitoring. Ensure capacity, prioritization, and flawless execution to meet program milestones, product disposition, client commitments, and uninterrupted supply.
* Govern the analytical method lifecycle from early development through transfer, qualification, validation, comparability, continued performance verification, and retirement. Ensure control strategies and specifications evolve appropriately through clinical development, process performance qualification, launch, and sustained commercial supply.
* Set global expectations for current good manufacturing practice, applicable good laboratory practice principles, data governance, principles that ensure data are attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate and complete, laboratory investigations, out of specification and out of trend management, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, change control, and audit readiness. Lead enterprise strategy and executive response for regulatory inspections and critical client audits.
* Build and deliver the digital and technology roadmap for laboratory information management systems, electronic laboratory notebooks, laboratory execution systems, chromatography data systems, laboratory automation, advanced analytics, and instrument connectivity. Sponsor validated deployment, master‑data governance, cybersecurity, and adoption that improve right‑first‑time outcomes and cycle time.
* Direct enterprise Quality Control capacity planning, capital prioritization, make‑versus‑buy decisions, laboratory footprint strategy, and governance of external testing partners. Align resources and contingency plans with demand forecasts, technology transfers, new product introductions, and network resiliency needs.
* Establish enterprise metrics and management review for on‑time testing and release support, lead time, invalid results, out of specification and out of trend rates, investigation cycle time, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, stability execution, method performance, cost, and productivity. Drive risk‑based priorities, Lean practices, and cross‑site learning to deliver sustainable improvement.
* Serve as the senior Quality Control liaison for strategic clients, regulatory authorities, and executive governance. Translate complex laboratory, method, and compliance risks into clear business implications, negotiate technically sound solutions, and ensure commitments are realistic, documented, and delivered.
* Build and lead a global organization through senior leaders. Define capabilities and succession plans, develop technical career paths and communities of practice, and cultivate a culture of scientific rigor, transparency, accountability, inclusion, and proactive risk management.
* Own escalation and coordinated response for significant Quality Control events, laboratory constraints, critical data‑integrity concerns, assay failures, method or specification issues, and testing disruptions. Make or recommend risk‑based decisions on testing strategy, product impact, remediation, and continuity of supply.
* Perform other duties in support of the broader Global Quality strategy and company objectives.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline, with fifteen or more years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or contract development and manufacturing organization Quality Control; or a Master’s degree with ten or more years.
* Ten or more years of people leadership, including five or more years leading senior leaders with accountability for multiple laboratories, sites, or functional areas.
* Demonstrated leadership of Quality Control across development and commercial stages, including method transfer, qualification and validation, release and stability testing, microbiology, and environmental and utility monitoring.
* Proven experience with global regulatory inspections and client audits, and with complex out of specification, out of trend, data‑integrity, and laboratory‑compliance matters.
* Experience managing budgets, capital portfolios, headcount, capacity, external laboratories, and enterprise transformation in a matrixed global organization.
* Executive‑level communication and client‑facing experience in a regulated, technically complex environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced scientific degree and/or a Master of Business Administration.
* Global leadership within a contract development and manufacturing organization supporting biologics, vaccines, advanced therapies, or sterile manufacturing.
* Experience scaling Quality Control from clinical development through process performance qualification, launch, and sustained commercial supply.
* Working knowledge of the following: Food and Drug Administration; European Medicines Agency; Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency; Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency; International Council for Harmonisation guidelines Q2, Q5, Q6, Q9, Q10, and Q14; United States Pharmacopeia; European Pharmacopoeia; Japanese Pharmacopoeia; Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations Parts 210, 211, and 11; and European Union Good Manufacturing Practice Annexes 1 and 11; as well as applicable data‑integrity expectations.
* Experience deploying global laboratory information management systems and laboratory digitalization and automation.
* Credentials from the American Society for Quality, and training in Lean and Six Sigma or equivalent quality and operational excellence disciplines.

If you are a strategic, hands‑on executive who thrives at the intersection of science, operations, and leadership, we would love to hear from you. Apply today and help us raise the bar for quality worldwide.
 
 
The US salary range for this position is $272,000 to $325,000.  Pay within this range varies by work location and may also depend on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.
 
 
Our programs are designed to focus on maintaining and enhancing all pillars of health with a robust benefits package including medical, dental, vision and prescription drug coverage with the option of a Health Savings Account with company contributions. In addition, we offer an industry leading 401(k)savings plan, insurance coverage , employee assistance programs and various wellness incentives. We support life-work balance with paid vacation time, sick time, and company holidays. Explore a supportive environment that enriches both your personal and professional growth!
 
 
This is a global position that will support all our FUJIFILM Biotechnologies sites. Benefits and compensation will be governed by the location that you are based from and considered your home site.
 
 
As part of any recruitment process, FUJIFILM Biotechnologies collects and processes personal data relating to job applicants. The  or ganisation  is committed to being transparent about how it collects and uses that data  and to meeting its data protection obligations and may share this as part of the global recruitment process with hiring  managers in Europe and the United St ates.
 
 
To all agencies: Please, no phone calls or emails to any employee of FUJIFILM about this requisition. All resumes submitted by search firms/employment agencies to any employee at FUJIFILM via- email , the internet or in any form and/or method will be deemed the sole property of FUJIFILM, unless such search firms /employment agencies were engaged by FUJIFILM for this requisition and a valid agreement with FUJIFILM is in place. In the event a candidate who was submitted outside of the FUJIFILM agency engagement process is hired, no fee or payment of any kind will be paid.
 
 
**EEO Information**
Fujifilm is committed to providing equal opportunities in hiring, promotion and advancement, compensation, benefits, and training regardless of nationality, age, gender, sexual orientation or gender identity, race, ethnicity, religion, political creed, ideology, national, or social origin, disability, veteran status, etc.
 
 
**ADA Information**
If you require reasonable accommodation in completing this application, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participating in the employee selection process, please direct your inquiries to our HR Department (fdbglobaltalent@fujifilm.com).

records.title: Vice President of Quality
records.description:
We are partnering with a leading global prestige beauty and skincare company to identify a
**Vice President of Quality**
to lead its North American Quality organization.

This is a high-impact executive leadership opportunity for a commercially minded quality professional who can connect quality, regulatory compliance, manufacturing excellence, and business performance within a complex, global organization.

The successful candidate will oversee Quality across North American manufacturing and distribution operations, providing leadership to a network of internal manufacturing operations and external manufacturing partners across multiple continents.

**About The Opportunity**

Reporting into senior global leadership, the Vice President of Quality will lead an organization of approximately 100 professionals, with four Directors reporting directly into the role.

The scope encompasses contract manufacturing quality, factory quality (QA, QC, laboratories, and Quality Management Systems), and quality assurance across North America, while providing technical quality leadership and guidance to teams in Canada and Brazil.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Lead the North American Quality organization:**
 Provide strategic direction and leadership across manufacturing, quality assurance, quality control, laboratories, and quality systems.
* **Act as the business voice of Quality:**
 Partner with commercial, brand, manufacturing, and executive stakeholders to translate quality and regulatory requirements into sound business decisions.
* **Drive regulatory and compliance excellence:**
 Ensure alignment between global quality standards and US regulatory requirements, particularly FDA OTC regulations and Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).
* **Oversee contract manufacturing quality:**
 Provide quality leadership and oversight across a network of approximately 30–40 contract manufacturing partners, including key strategic suppliers.
* **Strengthen organizational capabilities:**
 Develop a technically strong team, promote greater autonomy, build leadership capabilities, and establish succession depth.
* **Partner with manufacturing leadership:**
 Work closely with plant and operational leaders to balance quality expectations with production demands, providing constructive challenge and driving continuous improvement.
* **Lead through influence:**
 Build strong relationships across a global, multicultural, and matrixed organization, including teams and stakeholders outside of the direct reporting structure.
* **Prepare the organization for future growth:**
 Build the organizational structure, capabilities, and relationships necessary to support a potentially broader international Quality remit.

**Ideal Candidate Profile**

* Extensive leadership experience in Quality within beauty, personal care, consumer health, or complex consumer goods manufacturing environments.
* Strong hands-on experience with
 **FDA OTC regulations and GMP requirements**
 .
* Proven experience leading large, multi-layered Quality organizations and developing senior leadership teams.
* Experience overseeing contract manufacturers, external manufacturing partners, and complex supplier networks.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing quality, QA, QC, laboratory operations, and Quality Management Systems.
* Commercially oriented leadership approach, with the ability to translate technical and regulatory considerations into practical business decisions.
* Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and operate effectively within global, matrixed organizations.
* Experience balancing quality standards, operational performance, and business priorities.
* Conversational French is considered a strong advantage.

records.description:
Responsible for maintaining the facilities system-wide Quality program; to include data collection, aggregating and analyzing data, maintaining policies and procedures. Facilitates alignment between improvement initiatives and the organizations strategic plan; directs the day-to-day execution of the strategies and tactic necessary to successfully improve the outcomes and results of the organization. M
OBIS Corporate Center America will be aiding in the hiring progress for this job position. 

*(*
*To perform within this position successfully, the incumbent must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Other duties may be assigned.)*

 

* Provide training and Guidance to QC and QA functions in their separate spheres of operations. Work with HOD’s / COD’s to establish long term goals for both departments.
* Ensure voice of the customer is heard by both groups and the rest of the organization.
* Interact with Senior Management at the OEM to understand their expectations and translate actionable activities within QC or QA as appropriate.
* Leads and is ultimately responsible for Quality (QA & QC) activities throughout the MOBIS Georgia plant.
* Ensure that projects are implemented in a timely manner and improvements are sustained by the organization.

 

**Quality Assurance & New Model Launch Management (MOBIS Product Development System / APQP)**

* Improvement of CS/RS related claims as well as quality cost.
* Manage monthly claim process, recall/campaign and service action.
* Manage external issues such as NHTSA , IQS/VDS, IATF, etc.
* Control internal communication with related teams about field issues

* KPI Management
* Profitability Improvement / Customer Incoming Quality (ppm) / Man Power (Salary & Hourly) / Policy Demerits (Customer Line Stop & Safety)

**Internal/External Quality Index Management**

* Internal/Customer Issue per day
* Supplier/Process Quality (ppm)
* Supplier Chargeback

**Supervisory Responsibilities:**

Yes

* Experience: 10 years
* Managerial Experience: 8+ years
* Education: Bachelor’s Degree (BA/BS) required, MBA desired
* Degree Field: Engineering, Quality, or related field.
* Equivalent Experience/Education: 15 years of experience in a manufacturing/automotive field
* Communication Skills: Advanced
* Mathematical Skills: Intermediate
* 5+ years of automotive Quality Assurance experience
* 5+ years of automotive Quality Control experience
* OEM or Tier 1 supplier manufacturing experience preferred.

**Required Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities:**

* Strategic Planning
* Operations Management
* Strategic Project Management
* Leadership
* People Management

records.title: Senior Manager, Product Development & Production
records.description:
Studs is a category-defining ear piercing and earring brand named one of "the 10 most innovative companies in retail for 2023" by Fast Company. Studs connects ear piercing with aftercare and earring shopping to create an end-to-end Earscaping® experience. We offer a better retail and digital experience that prioritizes safety and expertise in a cool, fun and welcoming environment, along with a wide earring assortment—all at an accessible price point.
 
 
The Senior Manager of Product Development & Production is responsible for execution of proposed product and design. They will take the product from the proposed design state to commercialization including physical product development and final production. They will also be responsible for building out a team org structure and training new team members
 
 
**Salary Range:**
$130,000
 
 
**Key Responsibilities:**
Product Development
 
 

* Establish strategic partnerships with suppliers, manufacturers, and other vendors in order to develop new products or improve existing products
* Oversee the product life cycle of new products from concept to commercialization
* Develop and manage the development calendar with milestones that aligns with the organization's strategic objective
* Manage all vendor WIPs, sample requests and inbound samples
* Price negotiation to achieve margin goals
* Work with external partners on brand collaboration products and key initiatives

Production
 
 

* Oversee production process from PO placement through ex-factory including vendor payment and credits
* Ensure bulk goods produced conform with approved designs and standards
* Set factory allocation to ensure they align with factories' capacity supporting the businesses growth and key initiatives
* Negotiate bulk inventory costs, lead times and deliveries
* Manage and resolve any manufacturing issues including delivery delays with factories
* Communicate delivery timelines and collaborate with cross functional partners on product launches

Testing & Relations
 
 

* Foster and maintain vendor relationships
* Lead on boarding process ensuring factory and vendor adherence to Stud's processes and standards, and that clear understanding of processes and nuances between vendors is maintained
* Develop and monitor, and continually improve quality assurance procedures and processes with external testing vendors
* Ensure all products manufactured that will be commercially sold are tested to STUDS standards prior to shipment
* Evaluate, improve, and define processes and policies, process implementation, and identify errors and areas of improvement
* Address the root causes of quality issues, create corrective action plans and implement long term solutions in partnership with external vendors

**Requirements:**

* 5+ years of experience in product development and/or production, with hands-on ownership of products from concept through bulk delivery.
* Jewelry experience strongly preferred, but not required. Experience in accessories or another consumer product category is a plus.
* Retail or DTC brand experience a plus, especially in a multi-channel business (physical retail and ecommerce).
* 2+ years of people management experience, or a demonstrated record of training and developing team members. Interest in building a team structure from the ground up.
* Proven track record managing overseas and domestic factory partners, including vendor onboarding, factory allocation, and capacity planning.
* Highly organized, with the ability to run a development calendar across many SKUs, vendors, and launches at once in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
* Clear, direct communicator who works well across functions, including Merchandising, Finance, Retail, and Marketing.
* Advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills. AI fluency preferred: comfortable using AI tools in daily work to move faster.
* Based in New York, NY and able to work from the HQ office on a hybrid schedule.
* Driven, creative problem solver that consistently acts with integrity and speaks up
* Owner's mindset, with the ability to approach feedback and problems with a positive attitude.

**Benefits & Perks**

* Flexible Work Environment (3 days in office, 2 days work from home)
* Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance (including a plan option with $0 in-network mental health visits)
* Access to Mental Health and Work/Life Resources including Online Therapy, Gender Affirmation Support Services, and Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Voluntary Life Insurance
* Health and Commuter Tax-Advantaged Accounts
* Stock Options in connection with the Company's Equity Incentive Plan
* 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan
* Paid Time Off, Paid Safe & Sick Leave, and Paid Parental Leave
* Paid Sabbatical After 4 Years of Service
* Exclusive Employee Discounts on Piercings and Jewelry (we've got your friends and family covered too!)
* Access to PerkSpot and additional benefits such as pet insurance, discounted tickets, personal finance coaching, healthy rewards, and more!

*Studs is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing a work environment that fosters diversity, inclusion, and equal opportunity without regard to race, color, gender, age, creed, sex, religion, national origin, disability (physical or mental), marital status, citizenship, ancestry, sexual orientation, gender identity and gender expression, or any other legally protected status. Studs considers qualified applicants with criminal histories. We comply with applicable state and local laws prohibiting discrimination in employment in every jurisdiction in which we operate. If you require an accommodation for the application process, please email HRBP@studs.com.*
*Massachusetts Applicants: It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.*
*Click here for the Studs Privacy Notice for California Applicants.*

records.title: Director - Corporate Continuous Improvement
records.description:
**Description**
****Position Summary****
The Director of Corporate Continuous Improvement (CI) leads MacAllister’s enterprise CI strategy, Corporate CI team, and improvement portfolio. In partnership with the owner, executive team, and divisional leaders, the Director helps establish and build alignment around MacAllister’s CI vision, strategy, priorities, and multi-year roadmap. The Director identifies and prioritizes high-value opportunities, builds organizational problem-solving capability, and leads improvement work from opportunity identification through execution and sustainment.
 
 
The role establishes CI standards, tools, and training; coaches, mentors, and influences leaders and teams across the organization; and communicates CI priorities, results, and opportunities for support.
 
 
The ultimate objective is to build and sustain a culture in which continuous improvement becomes habitual and is reflected in how leaders and employees think, act, solve problems, and improve the way work gets done.
 
 
****Position Duties/Responsibilities****
**Primary Responsibilities**

* Partner with the executive team, and divisional leaders to develop and maintain MacAllister’s CI strategy, multi-year roadmap, priorities, and operating model aligned with company goals. Build leadership alignment and shared ownership of CI priorities and expectations across the organization.
* Own CI project identification, prioritization, approval, execution, and close-out, focusing on where CI creates the most value; support employee-driven improvement alongside leader-sponsored initiatives.
* Maintain consistent project close-out documenting results, lessons learned, and sustainment plans; verify improvements and results are sustained and take corrective action as needed.
* Set organization-wide CI standards, tools, and terminology; guide Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, DMAIC, and PDCA application grounded in facts, data, and root cause analysis; coach project teams and facilitate select high-impact improvement events.
* Lead improvement-related change management, engaging affected employees early and ensuring process adoption and sustainment.
* Oversee CI training tailored to responsibility levels using consistent terminology and live projects; coach and support CI-trained departmental leaders who remain in their home departments outside CI.
* Define CI value primarily through capability measures—leaders solving problems independently, AI use cases adopted, and idea-to-approval cycle time—with financial results as supporting evidence.
* Communicate CI initiatives, results, and available support so leaders know when and how to engage the team; share success stories and recognize improvement contributors.
* Use coaching-first leadership to build team autonomy, confidence, and influence; foster problem reporting, experimentation, and learning from mistakes by supporting people publicly and coaching privately.
* Hire, develop, and manage CI personnel; oversee budget, resource allocation, and team structure as needs evolve.
* Play a leadership role in MacAllister’s Center of Practice for CI, AI, and problem-solving leadership, incorporating AI and other emerging technologies into CI methods where they improve problem solving, decision making, or productivity. Partner with MacAllister’s enterprise AI leadership on broader AI strategy, standards, and adoption.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**

* Directly supervises the Corporate CI team and oversees day-to-day operations of the CI department. Mentors and coaches CI team members to strengthen their capabilities as problem solvers, facilitators, coaches, and trusted business partners.
* Reviews and evaluates the work and performance of reporting employees; has authority for hiring and disciplinary actions.

****Position Requirements****
**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, or a related field.
* 10 years or more of experience in continuous improvement, operations, or business transformation.
* 5 years or more of experience leading leaders.
* Proven success coaching others to identify and solve problems independently.
* Working knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, DMAIC, and PDCA.
* A valid driver’s license.

**Preferred**

* Master’s degree in business or a related discipline.
* Lean Six Sigma Master Black Belt or equivalent depth of experience designing and delivering CI training.
* Experience at a Caterpillar dealership or in the equipment sales, service, or rental industry.
* Demonstrated curiosity and willingness to learn and apply emerging technologies, including AI, to strengthen problem solving, process improvement, decision support, and organizational productivity. Experience applying AI in these areas is preferred but not required.
* Experience building on an existing CI function and growing its influence across a multi-location organization.

****Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities****

* Strong coaching and leadership development skills; leads through influence rather than authority.
* Ability to connect improvement work to business priorities and help leaders choose where to focus.
* Curiosity about and practical comfort with AI as a business tool.
* Exceptional communication and facilitation skills with all levels, from the front line to executives.
* Ability to build and maintain trusted relationships with executives, senior managers, and teams.
* Respect for existing culture and relationships, with the judgment to improve without unnecessary disruption.
* Strong organizational, prioritization, and project management skills.
* Effective computer skills with Microsoft Office and the ability to learn proprietary systems.

****Other Requirements of Position****

* Works under broad supervision. Designs and carries out programs and far-reaching objectives independently, informing management as appropriate.
* Major responsibilities require a wide degree of creativity and latitude.
* If an error is made while in this position, it will require some effort to identify and can significantly impact the company financially.
* Frequently communicates with coworkers, customers, company executives, and management.
* Maintain equipment and supplies to avoid waste, damage to areas and equipment, and to prevent accidents.

The duties and responsibilities outlined in this posting are not exhaustive and may evolve based on business needs.
 
 
All MacAllister Machinery companies are an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer, including Disabled and Veteran applicants.

records.title: Director of Quality-Operations
records.description:
**About Us:**
BW Papersystems, part of the Barry-Wehmiller Group, builds capital equipment that transforms paper into products for consumers - every day, around the world. We offer innovative technologies, service and parts, and years of global experience in corrugating, finishing; slitting and packaging; stationery; bookbinding and security documents. Customers rely on our machines to produce and convert items such as corrugated boxes, folding cartons, passports, notebooks, copy paper, board, and coated and other specialty papers. For more information, visit bwpapersystems.com.
 
 
Barry-Wehmiller is a diversified global supplier of engineering consulting and manufacturing technology for the packaging, corrugating, sheeting and paper-converting industries. By blending people-centric leadership with disciplined operational strategies and purpose-driven growth, Barry-Wehmiller has become a $3 billion organization with nearly 12,000 team members united by a common belief: to use the power of business to build a better world.
 
 
**Job Description:**
The Director of Quality will be responsible for developing the overall Quality Improvement Strategy and lead the team in the cross-functional adoption and execution of that strategy. In this critical role, the Director of Quality will be the leader in developing and maintaining a quality management system to improve operating efficiency, quality and productivity in operations, to improve customer satisfaction, and to increase profitability in a safe working environment.
 
 
**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Develop the overall Quality Improvement Strategy and lead the management team in the cross-functional adoption and execution of that strategy.
* Develop and maintain a business/quality management system to improve operating efficiency, quality and productivity in operations, to improve customer satisfaction and increase profitability in a safe working environment within the local business.
* Continuously assess the overall Quality Management System, Quality Plan and Quality Organization to determine priorities for quality improvement.
* Establish the key improvement priorities, and using a strategy deployment approach, develop and execute a cross-functional, strategic action plan to drive improvement.
* Identify the leading sources of customer dissatisfaction.
* Determine the underlying causes and develop/execute strategies to eliminate those causes.
* Determine the true, systemic root causes of internal failure and Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ).
* Execute a strategy consisting of well-planned and executed preventive actions that reduce COPQ and other forms of waste.
* Drive improvements in process quality, production efficiency, and the elimination of the factors that drive variability and unforeseen disruptions.
* Drive a strategy that incorporates standard work, effective training, and recurring process audits to ensure process discipline.
* Establish and maintain appropriate KPIs that provide objective evidence of improvement
* Participate in training and coaching teams in the standard quality improvement approach and quality management standard requirements to develop organizational capability.

**EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE:**

* Bachelor’s degree in business, quality, continuous improvement, or related field.
* 10+ years of professional experience leading a Quality Organization in capital equipment manufacturing environment.
* Experience with the execution of continuous improvement methodology such as Operational Excellence, Lean Manufacturing, Strategy Deployment, etc.

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES:**

* Requires the ability to independently resolve complex problems.
* Requires ability to manage a skilled and diverse staff, communicate effectively, represent the organization, act decisively, and influence decisions of senior managers and customers.

records.title: Director of Process Engineering & Continuous Improvement
records.description:
The Director of Process Engineering & Continuous Improvement is the company's technical authority for how meals are made and the owner of its improvement engine. This hands-on leader combines deep manufacturing process engineering with a disciplined continuous improvement approach to make production operations more consistent, efficient, safe, and cost-effective across Mom's Meals.
 
 
The role will focus primarily on kitchen and production operations, supporting a highly automated manufacturing environment through process design, equipment performance, root cause problem solving, and structured improvement projects. The position will also support fulfillment operations by identifying automation and process opportunities that improve throughput, labor efficiency, accuracy, and customer service.
 
 
The Director partners closely with Production, Fulfillment, Supply Chain, Food Safety and Quality, Maintenance, R&D, IT, and Finance to execute strategic projects and deliver measurable, sustained improvement across the enterprise. This is a player-coach role: the Director is expected to engage directly on the production floor, lead technical problem solving, and develop the engineers and improvement practitioners on the team.
 
 
**This position will travel to our other facilities 25-50% at varying times.**
**Ideally, the selected candidate will work out of one of our Production facilities (Ankeny/Grinnell, IA, Oklahoma City, OK, or North Jackson, OH) but are open to remote for the right skills and experience.**
**Benefits**
Our employees enjoy a generous package of benefits that we are thrilled to provide, and feel is part of what makes us different as an employer. We value our team members, and this is one way we can show it.
 
 
**Benefits Include**

* PTO, holiday pay and holiday of choice
* 401(k) match
* Life insurance
* Short-term disability
* Health, dental and vision insurance
* Maternity/paternity leave
* Health savings account (HSA)
* Flex spending accounts (FSA) – health and dependent

**Position Responsibilities May Include, But Not Limited To**
Process & Technical Engineering
 
 

* Serve as the company's process authority for meal production, owning process design, line layouts, standard work, and process specifications for cooking, chilling, portioning, and packaging
* Lead structured process control plans, risk assessments, and capability studies to reduce variation and improve consistency
* Drive yield, discard, and portion-control improvements through engineering-based solutions
* Partner with Production, Food Safety and Quality, Maintenance and R&D teams to ensure process changes are validated, documented, and sustained on the production floor
* Reduce downtime and defects through root cause analysis and hands-on, engineering-based problem solving
* Evaluate emerging manufacturing technologies and process innovations that improve efficiency, quality, and scalability
* Ensure engineering and process solutions comply with USDA, FDA, food safety, sanitary design, and regulatory requirements

Continuous Improvement & Operational Excellence
 
 

* Build and lead a multi-site continuous improvement program, maintaining a prioritized project portfolio with defined savings targets validated with Finance
* Champion Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and structured problem-solving methodologies (such as A3, DMAIC, value stream mapping, changeover reduction, and standard work)
* Drive waste reduction, productivity improvement, and labor optimization initiatives
* Evaluate operational KPIs, including OEE, yield, labor productivity, and discards, and use data analytics to prioritize improvement opportunities
* Coach kitchen and production leaders and engineers in structured problem solving, and ensure improvements are standardized and sustained
* Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across operations

Kitchen & Production Engineering
 
 

* Lead engineering efforts supporting highly automated meal production operations
* Drive equipment performance, uptime, and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) improvements
* Identify ideal equipment required to produce Mom's Meals to specification at scale, including equipment that should be replaced or decommissioned and equipment that can deliver OEE improvements and a measurable return on investment
* Partner with Production leadership and Commercialization team to identify bottlenecks and improve throughput
* Lead facility expansion projects, line installations, equipment upgrades, and process redesign initiatives

Capital & Automation Projects
 
 

* Develop and manage the engineering capital plan, prioritizing projects by safety, quality, and measurable return
* Lead project prioritization, design, budgeting, vendor selection, implementation, and startup activities
* Ensure projects are completed safely, on time, and within budget
* Manage external engineering firms, contractors, equipment suppliers, and system integrators
* Build a practical, multi-year automation roadmap focused on productivity, yield, and labor efficiency
* Establish project governance, reporting, and post-implementation performance reviews

Maintenance & Reliability Partnership
 
 

* Partner with Maintenance leadership on standards for asset management, equipment lifecycle planning, and preventative, predictive, and reliability-centered maintenance practices
* Use maintenance KPIs, including downtime, PM completion rates, equipment failure rates, and maintenance costs, to prioritize engineering and improvement work

Leadership & Team Development
 
 

* Provide coaching, mentorship, and technical leadership to process engineering, continuous improvement, and engineering personnel
* Develop future engineering leaders, improvement practitioners, and technical subject matter experts
* Promote a culture focused on safety, engagement, accountability, and operational excellence

**Required Skills And Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field
* 10+ years of progressive engineering leadership experience within manufacturing, food production, and highly automated operations, including leading process engineering or continuous improvement teams
* Hands-on experience applying Lean and Six Sigma tools, with a demonstrated record of delivering quantified, sustained savings and performance gains
* Strong process engineering skills, including process design, root cause analysis, process capability, statistical analysis, and OEE and yield analytics
* Demonstrated success leading capital projects and automation implementations, including equipment installations and line upgrades
* Working knowledge of industrial automation, controls, packaging systems, and manufacturing technologies
* Knowledge of Sanitary Design Principles and Standards for food manufacturing.
* Experience leading teams in regulated manufacturing environments
* Proven ability to influence cross-functional leaders and drive enterprise-wide change

**Preferred Skills And Experience**

* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification
* Food manufacturing, packaged goods, pharmaceutical, and automated distribution experience
* Experience with Industry 4.0 technologies, predictive maintenance, and digital manufacturing tools
* Experience managing and understanding facility utility controls, including HVAC, water, and steam systems
* Professional Engineer (PE) license or advanced technical degree

**Physical Requirements**

* Regularly required to use hands to feel, grab, or operate objects, tools, and controls while reaching with hands and arms
* Frequently required to stand, communicate, and listen
* Occasionally required to walk, stoop, kneel or crouch
* Occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds
* Visual perception to perform job including peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus
* Able to perform repetitive movements
* Able to work in variable temperatures (cold/hot)

**Company Overview**
Mom’s Meals is a home-delivered meal service providing fully prepared, refrigerated meal solutions direct to homes nationwide since 1999. We provide seniors, patients recovering post-discharge and those managing a chronic condition with tailored nutrition solutions to manage their specific needs. If you are passionate about the well-being of others and have a strong sense of community, Mom’s Meals could be the place for you! We are a family operated business looking for fun, compassionate, and friendly people who want to make a difference in the lives of others.
 
 
**EEO**
Mom’s Meals complies with all applicable federal and state non-discrimination laws. Qualified applicants shall receive consideration for employment without regards to race, religion, national origin, ancestry, color, gender, age, disability, or veteran status.

records.title: Director of Continuous Improvement
records.description:
**Job Description**
**About the role**
As the Director of Continuous Improvement, you’ll be the senior strategic leader driving operational excellence, transformation, and sustainable performance improvement across the enterprise. You’ll own the development, deployment, and governance of TERREPOWER’s global continuous improvement (CI) strategy — aligning it with business objectives and building a culture of innovation, accountability, and measurable results. It’s a high-impact role for a visionary change agent with deep Lean and Six Sigma expertise who can influence at every level and deliver real impact across diverse regions and functions.
 
 
**What You’ll Do**

* Strategic leadership — Define and execute a global CI strategy aligned with corporate goals, partner with executive leadership to identify high-value transformation opportunities, and establish enterprise-wide CI governance, frameworks, and performance standards.
* Operational excellence — Lead global CI initiatives using Lean, Six Sigma, and other methodologies, standardize processes and best practices across regions, and drive measurable improvements in cost, quality, delivery, safety, and customer satisfaction.
* Change management & culture — Champion a culture of continuous improvement and data-driven decision-making, and build organizational capability through training, coaching, and certification programs.
* Performance management — Develop KPIs, dashboards, and reporting to track CI progress and ROI, run regular reviews with regional and functional leaders, and benchmark best practices to maintain competitive advantage.
* Team leadership — Develop regional CI teams and leaders, foster collaboration across geographies and business units, and drive talent development and succession planning.

**What You’ll Bring**
**Must-haves**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Business, Operations, or a related field.
* 10+ years in continuous improvement, operational excellence, or transformation leadership, with proven success leading global or multi-site CI programs.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Master Black Belt certification.
* Strong analytical, strategic-thinking, and problem-solving skills.
* Exceptional communication and stakeholder-influencing abilities across all levels of an organization.

**Nice-to-haves**

* Master’s degree (MBA or related discipline).
* Experience in sustainable manufacturing, supply chain, and/or complex global operations.
* Expertise in digital transformation, automation, or advanced analytics.
* Track record of delivering significant financial and operational impact.

**What We Offer**

* Compensation — Competitive base salary plus annual performance bonus.
* Health & wellness — Medical, dental, and vision coverage.
* Retirement — 401(k) with company match.
* Time off — Paid time off, holidays, and parental leave.

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
**Director of Operations – Beauty & Cosmetics Manufacturing**

**Lead. Innovate. Transform.**

**Location:**
Azusa, CA | On-Site

**Salary Range:**
$130,000 – $160,000 annually, depending on experience (DOE)

**Reports Directly to the CEO**

**Ready to Lead the Next Chapter of Manufacturing Excellence?**

At Westwood Laboratories, we're building the future of our operations, and we're looking for a
**driven, hands-on Director of Operations**
to help lead the transformation.

As an established FDA-registered contract manufacturer specializing in beauty, cosmetics, personal care, and OTC products, we're focused on strengthening operational excellence, embracing technology, and building scalable processes for continued growth.

**We're not looking for someone to simply manage operations. We want someone who can elevate them.**

This is a high-impact leadership opportunity for someone who thrives in a fast-paced, evolving environment, takes ownership, and knows how to turn challenges into results.

**What You'll Lead**

* **Operational Excellence:**
 Oversee Production, Compounding, Warehouse, and Facilities, driving efficiency, quality, productivity, and cost improvements.
* **Quality & Compliance:**
 Champion a quality-first culture, ensuring manufacturing operations consistently meet cGMP, FDA, safety, and customer requirements. Partner closely with Quality and Regulatory teams to strengthen compliance, process controls, and right-first-time execution.
* **KPIs & Accountability:**
 Establish meaningful performance metrics, dashboards, and systems that drive measurable results.
* **Digital Transformation:**
 Lead the transition from paper-based processes toward automation, improved ERP utilization, and data-driven operations.
* **People Leadership:**
 Develop high-performing teams, strengthen accountability, and create a culture of ownership and continuous improvement.
* **Strategic Execution:**
 Partner directly with the CEO to translate business priorities into action, lead cross-functional projects, and deliver results.
* **Continuous Improvement:**
 Implement Lean manufacturing practices, reduce downtime and waste, and optimize production performance.

**What You Bring**

* **Direct manufacturing experience in beauty, cosmetics, or personal care is essential.**
* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing experience with strong operations leadership.
* Proven success implementing KPIs, improving processes, and driving measurable operational improvements.
* Experience with ERP systems, manufacturing automation, and organizational transformation.
* **Strong experience operating in FDA-regulated, cGMP manufacturing environments**
 , with a demonstrated understanding of quality systems, compliance, documentation, deviation management, CAPA, and process controls.
* Strong knowledge of Lean manufacturing, cGMP, and FDA-regulated operations.
* A self-motivated, solutions-oriented leadership style with strong project management and execution skills.
* A hands-on, solutions-oriented leadership style with the confidence to make decisions, drive accountability, and collaborate directly with executive leadership

**Why Westwood?**

Because you'll have the opportunity to make a real impact.

We're a company with a strong foundation and an exciting opportunity ahead. You'll work directly with the CEO, influence operational strategy, develop teams, and help shape the next phase of our growth.

**If you're a builder, a problem-solver, and a leader who gets things done, we want to hear from you.**

**Apply today and help us take Westwood Laboratories to the next level.**

*Westwood Laboratories is an Equal Opportunity Employer.*

records.description:
**Job Description**
**Honeywell Aerospace**
is a leading provider of innovative aerospace products and services. Our products and solutions are found on virtually every commercial, defense, and space aircraft in the world. We are committed to delivering cutting-edge technologies that enhance the safety, efficiency, and performance of the aerospace industry. Our aerospace business unit encompasses a wide range of products and services, including aircraft engines, cockpit and cabin electronics, wireless connectivity systems, mechanical components, and more. We are at the forefront of advancements in aviation technology, constantly pushing the boundaries to create healthier air travel, more fuel-efficient aircraft, and safer skies.
 
 
With our high-speed Wi-Fi offerings, we enable seamless connectivity for passengers and crew, enhancing the in-flight experience and enabling real-time data transmission. Our solutions also contribute to more direct and on-time flight arrivals, improving overall travel efficiency. In addition to our core products, we provide value-adding services such as maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) to ensure the continued reliability and performance of aerospace systems. Our facilities and expertise support the Federal government and agencies, further strengthening our position in the aerospace industry.
 
 
At Honeywell Aerospace, we are committed to sustainability and environmental responsibility. We strive to develop technologies that reduce emissions, improve fuel efficiency, and minimize the environmental impact of aviation. With revenues of $17.5 billion in 2025 and approximately 21,000 employees globally, we are a key player in the aerospace industry. Our dedicated team of professionals works tirelessly to introduce state-of-the-art technology solutions that drive efficiency, productivity, and safety in high-growth businesses.
 
 
As an
**Aerospace Operating System Site Leader**
here at Honeywell Aerospace, you will be a critical leader in the development and site-wide deployment for the Aerospace Operating System (AOS), driving the transformation of operational performance across the site or multi sites.
 
 
You will partner closely with Site Leader and AOS Global Operations Leader to establish the AOS roadmap, align strategic priorities, and enable scalable implementation across functions within the site including but not exclusive to planning, materials, sourcing, and quality.
 
 
As the key thought leader and change agent, this individual will coach leaders, drive method development and continuous improvement initiatives, and optimize end-to-end supply chain processes spanning procurement, planning, production, distribution, and logistics to support long-term growth, operational efficiency, and cultural transformation.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

**Job Description**
**Honeywell Aerospace**
is a leading provider of innovative aerospace products and services. Our products and solutions are found on virtually every commercial, defense, and space aircraft in the world. We are committed to delivering cutting-edge technologies that enhance the safety, efficiency, and performance of the aerospace industry. Our aerospace business unit encompasses a wide range of products and services, including aircraft engines, cockpit and cabin electronics, wireless connectivity systems, mechanical components, and more. We are at the forefront of advancements in aviation technology, constantly pushing the boundaries to create healthier air travel, more fuel-efficient aircraft, and safer skies.
 
 
With our high-speed Wi-Fi offerings, we enable seamless connectivity for passengers and crew, enhancing the in-flight experience and enabling real-time data transmission. Our solutions also contribute to more direct and on-time flight arrivals, improving overall travel efficiency. In addition to our core products, we provide value-adding services such as maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) to ensure the continued reliability and performance of aerospace systems. Our facilities and expertise support the Federal government and agencies, further strengthening our position in the aerospace industry.
 
 
At Honeywell Aerospace, we are committed to sustainability and environmental responsibility. We strive to develop technologies that reduce emissions, improve fuel efficiency, and minimize the environmental impact of aviation. With revenues of $17.5 billion in 2025 and approximately 21,000 employees globally, we are a key player in the aerospace industry. Our dedicated team of professionals works tirelessly to introduce state-of-the-art technology solutions that drive efficiency, productivity, and safety in high-growth businesses.
 
 
As an
**Aerospace Operating System Site Leader**
here at Honeywell Aerospace, you will be a critical leader in the development and site-wide deployment for the Aerospace Operating System (AOS), driving the transformation of operational performance across the site or multi sites.
 
 
You will partner closely with Site Leader and AOS Global Operations Leader to establish the AOS roadmap, align strategic priorities, and enable scalable implementation across functions within the site including but not exclusive to planning, materials, sourcing, and quality.
 
 
As the key thought leader and change agent, this individual will coach leaders, drive method development and continuous improvement initiatives, and optimize end-to-end supply chain processes spanning procurement, planning, production, distribution, and logistics to support long-term growth, operational efficiency, and cultural transformation.

* Business fluent in local language and English

* Ability to travel to other locations for training or project support (limited)

**WE VALUE**

* A Master of Business Administration is a plus
* Experience in various areas of operations is strongly preferred, i.e. production, planning, procurement, logistics or similar
* Successful track record in leading without formal authority
* Proven experiences in driving results & coaching teams/peers across departments
* Experience in developing and sustaining networks / communities
* Leadership qualities & experience in motivating and developing diverse teams
* 8 Years of Practical experience facilitating improvement events

* Passionate about learning Aerospace OS Core Methods and tools
* Results & quality orientation
* Methodical & structured way of thinking
* High analytical capability

records.description:
**Job Description**
**Company Overview**
Vertex is a global biotechnology company focused on investing in scientific innovation to create transformative medicines for people with serious diseases. Across our organization, we work with urgency, rigor, and collaboration to deliver therapies that improve patient outcomes and create long-term value.
 
 
**General Summary**
The Operational Excellence team serves as the process improvement and performance enablement backbone of CMTO, providing the improvement discipline, management systems, and change capabilities required to run, grow, and optimize Vertex’s commercial manufacturing network.
 
 
The Director, Operational Excellence leads the development and execution of CMTO’s Operational Excellence strategy and improvement portfolio. The role identifies and prioritizes performance improvement opportunities, leads structured problem-solving and transformation initiatives, and ensures improvements are implemented and sustained through effective change management, standard work, performance monitoring, and leadership accountability.
 
 
The Director also leads and develops the Operational Excellence team, building organizational capability, setting priorities, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and accountability. The role partners closely with Business Analytics, Network Performance, Manufacturing Operations, MS&T, Business Operations Leads, Quality, Supply Chain, and Finance to use performance insights to identify improvement priorities and deliver measurable business outcomes.
 
 
**Key Duties And Responsibilities**

* Operational Excellence Strategy & Initiative Execution
* Contribute to setting CMTO's operational excellence strategy, priorities, and success measures, aligned to enterprise and functional priorities
* Identify, prioritize, and drive execution of a portfolio of commercial manufacturing improvement and transformation initiatives — partnering with sites and functions while avoiding ownership of routine operations
* Lead initiatives targeting lead-time reduction, launch optimization, yield, and manufacturing success-rate improvements and COGM reduction through structured problem definition, root-cause analysis, options analysis, and ROI calculation
* Lead Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, and structured problem-solving initiatives across technical and business processes
* Develop clear business cases, recommendations, and implementation plans for Operational Excellence initiatives, including expected benefits, resource requirements, risks, and measures of success.
* Manage and Lead the Operational Excellence Team
* Establish and communicate a clear vision, mission, and strategic direction for the Operational Excellence team, ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and stakeholder expectations
* Partner with senior leadership to define team priorities, continuously reassessing and adjusting focus based on evolving business needs, operational risks, and strategic objectives
* Set clear performance expectations, goals, and development plans for team members; monitor progress, provide timely feedback, and hold the team accountable for results
* Remove organizational barriers and resolve escalated issues that impede team performance or delivery of key initiatives
* Foster a culture of continuous improvement, collaboration, innovation, and accountability by coaching and mentoring team members in problem-solving, communication, and leadership skills
* Build organizational capability by identifying skill gaps, developing talent, and implementing training and succession plans that strengthen Operational Excellence competencies
* Communicate team objectives, progress, achievements, risks, and resource needs to senior leadership and key stakeholders, ensuring transparency and alignment across organization
* Promote cross-functional collaboration and strong stakeholder relationships to enable successful execution of Operational Excellence initiatives and sustainable business improvements
* Continuous Improvement & Change Execution
* Embed structured problem-solving, continuous improvement, and change execution into CMTO governance and operating rhythms, using performance insights provided by Business Analytics, Network Performance, and functional teams.
* Ensure improvements are implemented and sustained through effective change management, standard work, control plans, performance monitoring, and clear process ownership.
* Identify and deploy digital tools, automation, and process solutions that improve operational performance and the scalability of Operational Excellence practices.
* Community of Practice & Capability Building
* Operate as a community-of-practice leader for manufacturing operational excellence across internal manufacturing and supply chain, driving common standards, methods, and ways of working
* Mentor teams on Lean methods, structured problem-solving, and continuous improvement practices, and benchmark industry best practices to inform innovative approaches

**Knowledge And Skills**

* Strong leadership, communication, collaboration, and team building
* Proven ability to motivate teams and build team unity
* Demonstrated success implementing Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, FMEA, Hoshin Kanri, and Change Management methodologies in GMP environments
* Proven experience leading improvement initiatives targeting lead-time reduction, launch optimization, yield improvement and COGM/COGs reduction
* Experience using operational data and performance insights to identify, prioritize, and measure improvement opportunities.
* Hands-on proficiency in data analysis, root-cause analysis, process analysis, and structured problem-solving
* Ability to quantify the operational and financial benefits of improvement initiatives and communicate clear recommendations to senior stakeholders.
* Experience implementing and sustaining performance management systems, visual management, Standard Work, and Leader Standard Work.
* Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word; experience with process mapping, statistical analysis, and Lean Six Sigma tools preferred.
* Ability to translate complex operational problems into clear improvement priorities, recommendations, and implementation plans.
* Ability to operate effectively in a matrixed environment with strong role clarity, partnering across Network Performance, Business Operations, Manufacturing Operations, MS&T, Finance, and Strategic Sourcing

**Education And Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Life Sciences, Business, or a related field required; advanced degree preferred.
* Typically requires 8–12 years of experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, regulated manufacturing, supply chain, MS&T, Operational Excellence, or business transformation environments.
* Minimum 5 years of experience leading Operational Excellence, transformation, continuous improvement, or complex process-improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrated experience leading and developing teams.
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt required

At Vertex, we embrace continuous learning and encourage employees to stay informed on advances in AI, technology, automation, and industry trends. We seek talent who bring an external perspective, demonstrate curiosity and sound judgment, and thoughtfully adopt new capabilities that improve decision-making, drive innovation, increase efficiency, and help deliver better outcomes for patients.
 
 
**Pay Range**
$181,900 - $272,900
 
 
**Disclosure Statement**
The range provided is based on what we believe is a reasonable estimate for the base salary pay range for this job at the time of posting. This role is eligible for an annual bonus and annual equity awards. Some roles may also be eligible for overtime pay, in accordance with federal and state requirements. Actual base salary pay will be based on a number of factors, including skills, competencies, experience, and other job-related factors permitted by law.
 
 
At Vertex, our Total Rewards offerings also include inclusive market-leading benefits to meet our employees wherever they are in their career, financial, family and wellbeing journey while providing flexibility and resources to support their growth and aspirations. From medical, dental and vision benefits to generous paid time off (including a week-long company shutdown in the Summer and the Winter), educational assistance programs including student loan repayment, a generous commuting subsidy, matching charitable donations, 401(k) and so much more.
 
 
**Flex Designation**
Hybrid-Eligible Or On-Site Eligible
 
 
**Flex Eligibility Status**
In this Hybrid-Eligible role, you can choose to be designated as:
 
 

* Hybrid: work remotely up to two days per week; or select
* On-Site: work five days per week on-site with ad hoc flexibility.

Note: The Flex status for this position is subject to Vertex’s Policy on Flex @ Vertex Program and may be changed at any time.
 
 
**Company Information**
Vertex is a global biotechnology company that invests in scientific innovation.
 
 
Vertex is committed to equal employment opportunity and non-discrimination for all employees and qualified applicants without regard to a person's race, color, sex, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital status, or any characteristic protected under applicable law. Vertex is an E-Verify Employer in the United States. Vertex will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law.
 
 
Any applicant requiring an accommodation in connection with the hiring process and/or to perform the essential functions of the position for which the applicant has applied should make a request to the recruiter or hiring manager, or contact Talent Acquisition at ApplicationAssistance@vrtx.com

records.title: Corporate Director of Quality
records.description:
Take the next step with an exciting and growing company
 
As the only fully integrated maker of premium quality wire, rope, and assemblies, Loos & Co holds a leading position in the global aerospace sector.
 
A division of the Central Wire (CWI) Group of Companies encompassing 12 locations in three countries, 750+ employees, and over six decades of excellence, Loos & Co solutions are found in mission critical flight control applications. Our precision-manufactured components are also used for defense, med tech, and heavy industry purposes around the world, in large part because of the people behind our products.
 
Do you have a strong work ethic? Take pride in a job well done? Are you passionate about contributing to individual and team, company and customer successes? If you’re interested in joining a dynamic work environment that offers opportunities to reach your full potential, we want to hear from you.
 
 
Position Summary / Essential Function
 
The Corporate Director of Quality is CWI’s senior enterprise Quality leader and is responsible for establishing and sustaining a culture of quality excellence, accountability, customer focus, product safety, and continuous improvement across aerospace, commercial, medical, metal rope, and assembly facilities. Based in Pomfret Center, Connecticut and reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director leads the enterprise Quality function, develops high-performing teams of Quality professionals, and establishes the governance, systems, standards, metrics, and decision rights required for consistent execution across all locations.
 
A central responsibility of the role is to create a results- and data-driven culture in which decisions are based on objective evidence, process capability, customer and regulatory requirements, risk, and measurable business outcomes. The Director advances the organization from reactive inspection and problem resolution toward prevention, disciplined problem solving, statistical thinking, robust corrective action, and sustained operational excellence.
 
The Director maintains the effectiveness and certification readiness of applicable quality management systems, including AS9100D and ISO 9001 for aviation, space, defense, and commercial operations; ISO 13485 for medical-device operations where applicable; and customer-, product-, and facility-specific requirements for metal rope, wire rope, cable, and assemblies. The role ensures that customer and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements take precedence where they exceed or conflict with general quality-system requirements.
 
Key Responsibilities
 

* Build, lead, develop, and retain a high-performing organization of Quality professionals across CWI, with clear roles, decision rights, measurable objectives, development plans, succession pipelines, and performance expectations.
* Create a results- and data-driven culture of Quality excellence in which teams use objective evidence, trend analysis, statistical methods, and risk-based thinking to identify priorities, prevent defects, and verify sustained improvement.
* Establish and execute the enterprise Quality strategy, organizational design, staffing plan, technical roadmap, and resource priorities in alignment with CWI business and operating objectives.
* Own enterprise governance for quality management systems and maintain certification readiness for applicable aerospace, commercial, medical, metal rope, and assembly facilities, including registrar, customer, regulatory, and internal audits.
* Ensure aerospace quality controls address AS9100D requirements, including operational risk management, configuration management, product safety, counterfeit-parts prevention, special-process control, production process verification, foreign-object damage prevention, traceability, and awareness of ethical behavior.
* Ensure first article inspection and production process verification practices align with AS9102 when contractually applicable, and ensure special processes are qualified, controlled, and approved to customer, regulatory, or other requirements where applicable.
* Ensure medical quality-system controls align with ISO 13485 and applicable regulatory and customer requirements, including risk management, validated processes, traceability, complaint handling, CAPA, change control, and record retention.
* Establish common standards for document and record control, calibration, inspection and test, nonconforming output, CAPA, root-cause analysis, internal auditing, management review, supplier quality, customer complaints, product and process change control, and continuous improvement.
* Establish an enterprise Quality performance-management system with leading and lagging indicators for customer complaints, escapes, first-pass yield, scrap and rework, cost of poor quality, supplier defects, audit findings, process capability, CAPA aging, recurrence, and corrective-action effectiveness.
* Lead monthly operating reviews and formal management reviews that convert Quality data into executive-level insights, identify systemic and emerging risks, assign accountable owners, and track actions through verified closure.
* Develop Quality leaders who can influence Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Commercial teams; make risk-based decisions; escalate product-safety or conformity concerns; and hold the organization accountable for results.
* Serve as the senior Quality escalation point for significant customer complaints, product escapes, product-safety events, audit findings, systemic nonconformances, supplier-quality issues, and certification or regulatory risks.
* Ensure robust containment, root-cause analysis, corrective action, effectiveness verification, and lessons-learned deployment for significant or recurring failures, including consideration of human factors where relevant.
* Provide enterprise oversight for supplier-quality strategy, supplier qualification, risk-based surveillance, source inspection, flow-down of customer and regulatory requirements, and supplier corrective action.
* Partner with the Chief Operating Officer, Plant Managers, Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Commercial, and other leaders to integrate Quality into operational performance, new-product introduction, manufacturing transfers, and change management.
* Communicate Quality-system health, certification status, customer performance, material risks, resource needs, and improvement results clearly to executive leadership and the Board or ownership group when requested.
* Perform other related duties consistent with the role, grade, and business needs.

Required Qualifications
 

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Materials Science, Metallurgy, Quality, Manufacturing, or a closely related technical discipline.
* Twelve or more years of progressive Quality, manufacturing, engineering, or operational leadership experience in regulated or high-reliability manufacturing.
* At least seven years of direct people-leadership experience, including leadership of Quality managers and professionals, performance management, coaching, organizational design, and succession planning.
* At least five years of multi-site or enterprise Quality leadership experience with accountability for common systems, audits, metrics, and cross-site standardization.
* Demonstrated responsibility for an AS9100D-certified quality management system and successful participation as the senior Quality leader in at least one third-party certification or recertification cycle.
* Demonstrated experience with internal and external audit programs, management review, CAPA, root-cause analysis, configuration and change control, supplier quality, product safety, traceability, nonconformance control, and customer complaint resolution.
* Demonstrated use of Quality data and statistical methods to improve performance, including examples of measurable reduction in defects, escapes, cost of poor quality, or recurring corrective actions.
* Ability to travel approximately 25% to 40% to CWI facilities, customer sites, supplier sites, and audit locations, with additional travel during significant launches, audits, or quality events.
* Ability to communicate technical and business risk, priorities, decisions, and performance clearly to plant, functional, customer, registrar, and executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications
 

* Experience in specialty metals, wire, cable, wire rope, aircraft cable, mechanical cable, swaging, metal assemblies, or other highly engineered metal products.
* Experience leading Quality in aerospace and defense manufacturing, including customer flow-downs, AS9102 first article inspection, source inspection, special processes, counterfeit-parts controls, configuration management, product safety, and foreign-object damage prevention.
* Experience with ISO 13485-certified medical-device manufacturing and risk-management practices aligned with ISO 14971 where applicable.
* Experience with Nadcap-accredited special processes, Defense Contract Management Agency oversight, Federal Aviation Administration-regulated products, or major aerospace prime and Tier 1 customer requirements, as applicable to CWI’s business.
* Advanced degree in Engineering, Operations, Quality, or Business Administration.
* Experience using an electronic QMS, ERP, business-intelligence, and statistical software to manage Quality performance and traceability.

Preferred Certifications
 

* ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE) or equivalent senior Quality leadership credential.
* ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), ASQ Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), or AS9100 Lead Auditor certification.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Master Black Belt.
* Certified Manufacturing Engineer, Professional Engineer, Project Management Professional, or comparable technical credential as relevant.

Key Leadership Competencies
 

* Enterprise Quality leadership and culture building
* Leadership, development, and retention of Quality professionals
* Results orientation and measurable accountability
* Data-driven decision making and statistical thinking
* AS9100D, ISO 9001, and regulated quality-system leadership
* Product safety, compliance, and risk-based judgment
* CAPA, root-cause analysis, and corrective-action effectiveness
* Customer quality and executive escalation
* Cross-functional influence and change leadership
* Continuous improvement and operational excellence
* Executive communication and management review
* Multi-site governance and standardization

Leadership Standard
 
Success in this position is measured not simply by maintaining certifications or passing audits, but by the Director’s ability to build capable Quality leaders and teams, establish measurable accountability, improve the effectiveness of CWI’s quality systems, reduce recurring failures and customer escapes, strengthen process capability, protect product safety and conformity, and demonstrate sustained improvement through objective performance data.
 
Physical and Work Environment Requirements
 
The role operates in office and active manufacturing environments and requires regular interaction with plant operations.
