Operating from its advanced manufacturing facility in Casper, Wyoming, Scottsdale Mint specializes in high-purity bullion, legal-tender coin programs, and custom-branded precious metal products. The company combines artistic design, scientific precision, and advanced minting technology to deliver products recognized for their quality, detail, and authenticity.

**Position Summary**

The Senior Manager of Operations is responsible for overseeing the daily performance and overall effectiveness of Scottsdale Mint's Coining, Melting, CNC Machining, and Die Manufacturing departments. This position provides leadership and direction to approximately 30 employees, ensuring manufacturing operations are safe, efficient, productive, and aligned with company objectives.

The successful candidate will be a visible, hands-on leader capable of managing multiple manufacturing functions, developing departmental supervisors, establishing accountability, and improving operational performance while supporting current production requirements and future manufacturing growth.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Manufacturing & Operations Management**

* Oversee daily operations and production performance across Coining, Melting, CNC Machining, and Die Manufacturing.
* Establish departmental priorities, production goals, and performance expectations in coordination with senior management.
* Coordinate labor, equipment, and resources to maximize productivity, throughput, and manufacturing capacity.
* Monitor production schedules and workflow, identifying bottlenecks and implementing solutions to improve output and efficiency.
* Coordinate with Planning & Inventory Control, Fulfillment, Maintenance, Marketing, and other departments to support production requirements and company objectives.
* Develop, monitor, and report on departmental KPIs to optimize workforce utilization and ensure production schedule adherence.

**2. Leadership & Workforce Management**

* Provide leadership, direction, and accountability to departmental supervisors and employees.
* Manage staffing levels, scheduling, attendance, and labor allocation to meet production requirements.
* Establish clear expectations for employee performance, productivity, communication, and workplace conduct.
* Conduct performance reviews, address personnel matters, and establish development objectives for direct reports.
* Develop supervisory capabilities and ensure employees receive appropriate training to perform their responsibilities effectively.
* Foster a professional work environment emphasizing teamwork, accountability, ownership, and employee development.

**3. Safety, Compliance & Operational Excellence**

* Maintain consistent operating standards, manufacturing procedures, and a strong safety culture across all assigned departments.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA regulations, company safety policies, and applicable workplace requirements.
* Monitor key performance indicators, including production output, labor efficiency, downtime, quality, and schedule attainment.
* Evaluate manufacturing processes to identify safety concerns, operational inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement.
* Promote proper equipment operation, preventative maintenance, housekeeping, and organization throughout manufacturing areas.
* Ensure operational and safety issues are addressed promptly and corrective actions are implemented.
* Communicate departmental performance, challenges, and improvement initiatives to senior management.

**Qualifications & Experience**

* 5–7 years of progressive manufacturing supervisory or management experience, preferably overseeing multiple departments.
* Experience managing production teams and workforces of approximately 25–50 employees preferred.
* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations Management, or a related discipline preferred; equivalent practical experience will be considered.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production workflows, labor management, and operational efficiency.
* Working knowledge of OSHA regulations and manufacturing safety requirements.
* Demonstrated ability to manage production objectives, develop supervisors, and hold employees accountable for performance.
* Strong organizational, problem-solving, and verbal and written communication skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and manufacturing-related reporting systems.

**Position Expectations**

The Senior Manager of Operations is expected to take ownership of the overall performance of the assigned manufacturing departments. This individual must provide consistent leadership, establish clear priorities, and ensure departmental supervisors are effectively managing their teams and achieving established objectives.

Success will be measured by the ability to meet production goals, maintain safe and efficient operations, effectively manage workforce resources, improve manufacturing performance, and develop a capable and accountable team.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee discount
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Paid time off
* Referral program
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Nice to Have

This position may require work hours outside of the regularly scheduled hours to meet operational needs. This may include work during evenings, weekends, and/or holidays. records.description:
### **Senior Manager, Operational Excellence - Factor US**

***This role is hybrid to our Goodyear, AZ Factor facility***

### **Company Overview**

At Factor, we are on a mission to revolutionize the way people eat by making healthy, fresh, chef-prepared meals accessible and effortless. As the market leader in the Ready-To-Eat (RTE) meal space, we eliminate the need for cooking and meal prep while delivering high-quality, nutrition-focused meals directly to millions of customers. The Factor team is diverse, high-performing, and fast-growing, offering an inspiring environment where process innovation, operational discipline, and continuous improvement thrive.

### **About the role**

The **Senior Manager, Operational Excellence** leads OpEx capability and multi-site improvement programs across Factor's US ready-to-eat fulfillment, production and distribution network. The role owns projects end to end, from charter and business case through delivery and post-mortem. It combines Lean and Six Sigma methods with senior project-management discipline.

You will serve as a lead advocate for operational transformation by partnering with and challenging business leaders to adopt systems thinking and continuous process innovation.

### **You will...**

* Lead strategic Factor operations projects in continuous improvement, change management, cost optimization and OpEx training across RTE fulfillment networks.
* Direct complex, cross-facility improvement programs, coordinating site leadership with central project teams.
* Own project governance end to end: find high-ROI opportunities, write financially justified charters and capital project justifications, negotiate resources, launch teams, track results and remove roadblocks.
* Deliver projects to demanding schedules and aggressive cost targets, often with changing requirements. Routinely assess project risks and identify alternative paths to offset them.
* Lead the cross-functional project prioritization workflow and scoping program, and facilitate the project pipeline for all stakeholders.
* Develop, improve and maintain the project management process for the organization, and ensure best practices are followed.
* Build organized project plans from complex inputs, track status across a large program, and keep accurate records through frequent iterations.
* Identify new technologies that can deliver meaningful benefits, and champion changes that drive measurable operational improvements.
* Oversee material handling equipment, automation and warehouse projects. Serve as liaison between vendors and site maintenance, operations and technology teams.
* Apply DMAIC, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping and 5-Why to eliminate root causes of operational friction.
* Lead change management and risk mitigation for key operational shifts.
* Capture and scale best practices across production and fulfillment sites.
* Mentor junior project managers, Lean practitioners and floor supervisors in complex system integrations, and provide leadership to assigned teams so key competencies are developed and maintained.
* Support COGS reporting and tool creation. Data-driven, sound bridges, and coordinate actions that reduce COGS.

### **You are...**

* **Strategic leadership:** Influences without direct authority and aligns multi-site leaders around shared operational goals.
* **Project and time management:** Delivers multi-phase process and infrastructure projects on time and within budget.
* **Organization:** Builds organized project plans from complex inputs and keeps accurate records across frequent iterations.
* **Enterprising and creative:** Starts new operational and strategic projects, and challenges conventional methods with new ideas.
* **Cross-functional collaboration**: Bridges Central Strategy, Food Safety & Quality Assurance, Logistics, Procurement and DC Operations.
* **Stakeholder facilitation:** Negotiates, facilitates and resolves conflicting priorities across local and central stakeholders.
* **Communication:** Independently manages the cadence of formal and informal communication across all levels of the organization.
* **Critical thinking:** Weighs the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions before committing.
* **Data-driven**: Interprets operational telemetry, unit economics and process-flow metrics to make decisions.
* **Coaching and mentorship:** Coaches floor supervisors, Lean practitioners and project managers with constructive, empathy-driven feedback.
* **Driven by results**: Pushes projects to completion with urgency, focused on tangible business outcomes.

### **You have...**

* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, or equivalent management experience.
* 7+ years of experience in continuous improvement / OpEx roles within food manufacturing, RTE operations, or cold-chain logistics.

records.description:
**Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality**

**Location:** Lakewood, Ohio  
**Company:** Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company  
**Employment Type:** Full Time  
**Reports To:** President

**About Ferry Cap**

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is a long-established American manufacturer of engineered fasteners and specialty metal components serving demanding industrial and power generation applications. As we invest in our people, equipment, and operating systems, we are seeking a senior quality leader who can help strengthen our processes and build a companywide culture of quality.

**Position Summary**

The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will lead Ferry Cap’s quality organization and serve as a key member of the company’s leadership team.

This is a hands on leadership position for someone with strong experience in metallurgy, metal transformation, manufacturing processes, and heat treatment. The successful candidate will work closely with operations, engineering, maintenance, supply chain, and customers to improve process control, solve technical problems, and ensure consistent product quality.

The right leader will view quality as an operating partnership, not simply an inspection function. This individual must be comfortable working on the production floor, engaging directly with employees, and helping build quality into every stage of the manufacturing process.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all quality assurance, quality control, laboratory, inspection, and quality systems activities.
* Partner directly with operations to establish a culture in which safety, delivery, quality, and cost are shared responsibilities.
* Provide technical leadership related to metallurgy, raw materials, metal forming, metal transformation, machining, threading, and heat treatment.
* Oversee metallurgical testing and analysis, including hardness, microstructure, case depth, decarburization, mechanical properties, material certification, and failure analysis.
* Evaluate and improve heat treatment processes, including furnace controls, quenching, tempering, process consistency, and product conformance.
* Strengthen incoming, in process, and final inspection systems to ensure product requirements are consistently achieved.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective action activities involving internal defects, customer complaints, supplier issues, and process failures.
* Use structured problem solving methods such as 8D, 5 Why, fishbone analysis, PFMEA, control plans, SPC, and MSA.
* Maintain and continuously improve the company’s quality management system, documentation, procedures, work instructions, and audit processes.
* Ensure compliance with customer requirements, industry standards, specifications, and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Lead customer audits, supplier audits, internal audits, and customer quality reviews.
* Build strong working relationships with customer quality and engineering teams.
* Develop meaningful quality metrics, including first pass yield, scrap, rework, cost of poor quality, customer complaints, corrective action effectiveness, and supplier performance.
* Improve material traceability and process control throughout the manufacturing operation.
* Lead supplier quality development and ensure purchased materials and outside processes meet Ferry Cap requirements.
* Develop, coach, and hold accountable the quality team while strengthening quality knowledge throughout the organization.
* Support new product introduction, process changes, capital projects, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Establish clear containment, escalation, and corrective action processes when quality concerns arise.

**Required Qualifications**

* Significant quality leadership experience in a metal manufacturing environment.
* Strong practical knowledge of metallurgy, material properties, metal transformation, and heat treatment.
* Experience with manufacturing processes such as cold forming, forging, machining, threading, rolling, or similar metalworking operations.
* Demonstrated ability to diagnose metallurgical and manufacturing process failures.
* Experience leading quality systems, customer audits, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.
* Strong working knowledge of dimensional inspection, mechanical testing, metallurgical testing, calibration, and measurement systems.
* Experience using quality tools such as PFMEA, control plans, SPC, MSA, 8D, and root cause analysis.
* Proven ability to work collaboratively with operations and engineering teams.
* Strong leadership, communication, organization, and problem solving skills.
* Willingness to spend significant time on the manufacturing floor and become personally involved in resolving issues.
* Bachelor’s degree in metallurgy, materials science, engineering, manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant manufacturing experience.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Ten or more years of progressive quality experience, including at least five years in a leadership role.
* Experience with engineered fasteners, high strength components, critical industrial products, or power generation applications.
* Experience with ISO based quality management systems and customer specific quality requirements.
* Experience working with commercial heat treat suppliers and internal heat treatment operations.
* ASQ certification, Six Sigma certification, or formal Lean manufacturing training.
* Experience working in a union manufacturing environment.

**Leadership Profile**

The successful candidate will be:

* Hands on and comfortable working directly with production employees.
* Collaborative and capable of building trust across departments.
* Technically strong, practical, and decisive.
* Focused on preventing defects instead of relying on inspection to find them.
* Comfortable challenging existing practices while respecting Ferry Cap’s people and history.
* Able to balance customer requirements with operational realities.
* Committed to accountability, continuous improvement, and developing others.

**Why Join Ferry Cap**

This position offers the opportunity to play a major role in the continued transformation and growth of a historic American manufacturing company. The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will have direct access to company leadership, meaningful influence over operations, and the opportunity to build a quality culture that supports Ferry Cap’s customers, employees, and long term success.

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

records.description:
**Director, Fund Operations**

**POSITION:** Full-time Exempt

**DEPARTMENT:** Impact Investing

**REPORTS TO:** Vice President, Impact Investing

**About the Organization**

**A FOUNDATION BUILT ON GREATER ATLANTA’S FUTURE**

The Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta is one of the nation’s largest community foundations, with over $1.7 billion in assets and more than seven decades of philanthropic leadership. Through grants, donor services, civic partnerships and impact investments, CFGA advances equity and opportunity across 23 counties in the Greater Atlanta region.

**The Role**

**BUILDING THE OPERATING FOUNDATION FOR IMPACT INVESTING**

The Director of Fund Operations will provide strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s impact investing fund platform. This role is responsible for strengthening and scaling the systems, processes, infrastructure, and controls necessary to support a growing and sophisticated investment portfolio. This person owns the end-to-end operating model for the Foundation's impact investment platform. This is a senior, hands-on role responsible for making sure that once an investment is approved, it closes, funds, is serviced and is reported on correctly, on time and with a clear record. The work spans closing, funding, servicing, fund administration, compliance, records, data and reporting. This role supports every fund and vehicle on the platform — including the GoATL Community Capacity Fund, GoATL Affordable Housing Fund, TogetherATL Affordable Housing Fund, GoATL Community Guarantee Pool, and the Atlanta Affordable Housing Fund — together with related joint ventures and special purpose entities.

In practice, this person is the platform’s operational backbone: the person who knows what each transaction and fund requires, organizes the people and documents needed to satisfy those requirements, maintains the authoritative record, anticipates deadlines and exceptions, and follows issues through to resolution. The Director does not practice law or make accounting or credit decisions. Instead, the role makes sure Legal, Finance and the investment team work together smoothly and that nothing falls through the cracks.

The Director works hand in hand with the Fund Accountant, Impact Investing, who sits in Finance. The Director owns the process and the operating record: deadlines, checklists, documents, vendor performance and the loan database. The Fund Accountant owns the books: the general ledger, fund financial statements, capital accounts, investor statements and audit work. The Director makes sure the right information arrives complete and on time; the Fund Accountant decides how it is recorded and signs off on the numbers.

The successful candidate will combine transaction discipline, financial fluency, legal-document literacy, systems thinking and persistent follow-through. This person must be comfortable moving between a closing checklist, a fund agreement, a late borrower report, a wire request, a reporting calendar and a vendor escalation without losing track of what the governing documents require or the record of what was done.

**Why This Role Matters**

The platform now manages more than 60 loans across multiple funds and vehicles and is preparing to deploy its next round of capital. It has outgrown a model in which staff fill each operational gap as it appears. This role will connect the investment team, Finance, Legal and outside providers into one way of working: smooth closings, consistent records, clear deadlines, and systems that hold what we know about each fund, relationship and investment, so that knowledge does not live only in people’s heads.

* Creates one accountable owner for the transaction and fund lifecycle after investment approval.
* Replaces informal handoffs and institutional memory with documented workflows, complete records, calendars, controls and escalation paths.
* Gives Finance (including the Fund Accountant, Impact Investing), Legal and Portfolio Management a disciplined operating counterpart while preserving their independent authority.
* Ensures outside administrators, servicers and specialists work as extensions of our own process, with the Foundation keeping ownership of its records and decisions.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

**WHAT YOU’LL DO**

**Transaction Closing and Funding Coordination**

* Own the closing process from approval through funding and loan setup with the servicer, maintaining a complete checklist of approval conditions, legal documents, due diligence, signatures, funding mechanics and post-closing items. Because real estate deals fund on the day of closing, every item, including the wire request, must be ready before signing day.
* Translate investment approvals and term sheets into coordinated workplans for the deal lead, Legal, Finance and the Fund Accountant, Treasury, the borrower and outside providers; surface conflicts, gaps and sequencing issues early.
* Coordinate document production and review, signature processes, lien and lender-agreement requirements, organizational documents, insurance, required consents and other closing deliverables. Track legal questions to formal resolution by counsel.
* Confirm that every funding and wire request is complete before it goes to Finance or Treasury: required approvals are in place, the borrower’s wire instructions have been verified by a phone call, and two people are involved in every wire. Maintain the standard wire request form used for both closings and construction draws.
* Ensure each closed transaction is set up accurately and handed off to the assigned portfolio owner with final documents, payment terms, covenants, reporting obligations, draw requirements and key dates recorded in the system of record under the loan’s ID.
* Give the Fund Accountant the final executed terms, funded amounts and key dates for each closing, so the loan is set up in the books from the same record.

**Fund and Entity Operations**

* Manage operating calendars and workflows for each fund, entity and capital source, including capital calls, distributions, investor onboarding, bank account administration (account openings and authorized signers), subscriptions, side letters, governance actions and record retention. The Fund Accountant calculates investor allocations, capital accounts and distribution amounts and records them; this role runs the calendar, notices and documents around them.
* Own a single, current investor contact list, including financial advisors and fund administrator portal access, so that capital call notices, reports and distributions reach the right people.
* Maintain one register of what each fund is required to do under its governing agreements, side letters, policies, approval authorities and committee actions; coordinate implementation with the accountable business, Legal and Finance owners.
* Track state filings, annual report deadlines and registered-agent requirements across all entities, and support General Counsel as needed in preparing and completing these filings. General Counsel owns legal and state filings and Finance owns tax and regulatory filings; this role keeps one shared calendar for all of them.
* Support cash forecasting and liquidity planning by giving the Fund Accountant and the Vice President, Impact Investing expected closing, draw and repayment dates, while preserving Finance's authority over cash, treasury policy and accounting treatment.
* Support Finance-led annual audits and tax work by gathering key information and answering common requests. The Fund Accountant manages the audit and the auditor relationship, and Finance keeps ownership of audit and tax strategy, filings and sign-off. Organize valuations and other fund-level deliverables by assembling source materials, tracking deadlines, coordinating responses and driving open items to resolution.

**Servicing and Portfolio Operations**

* Own the operational relationship with loan servicers and administrators, including billing, payment processing, notices, escrows, statements, payoff calculations, deadline reminders and follow-up on exceptions.
* Ensure payments, draws, amendments, waivers, modifications and payoff activity are documented, routed and recorded consistently. Escalate issues that stay unresolved and any service failures.
* Run the quarterly borrower reporting process: track whether each report has arrived and is complete, send notices when reports are late or missing pieces, and make sure reviewed figures are recorded in the system of record.
* Keep the calendar for annual affordability compliance reviews (rents, incomes and other terms required by each loan’s affordability restrictions) and loan maturities, so reviews by asset managers happen on schedule.
* Coordinate operational support for loans in workout or needing special attention, including document collection, approval tracking, counsel coordination and implementation of authorized actions.
* Distinguish operational monitoring from credit judgment: route substantive covenant, borrower-performance and risk matters to Portfolio and Asset Management and track resulting actions to completion.

**Data, Records and Reporting Infrastructure**

* Carry out the platform’s plan to move from scattered files and systems (including Foundant, SharePoint, Excel, the DocuSign data room, and the fund administrator’s Egnyte and Salesforce portal) to a single system of record, working with Investment, Finance, Legal, IT and the fund administrator.
* In coordination with IT and third-party partners, establish and maintain the system of record (a loan database) for fund, investor and transaction information, with clear ownership, access controls, shared IDs, naming standards and a full history of changes. Key terms lock at closing and change only through a dated, approved modification.
* Work with IT to build and maintain automated workflows (for example, in Power Automate) that move data between systems, send deadline alerts and refresh Power BI dashboards, and use AI tools to prepare summaries and checks for staff to review. Coordinate with the Fund Accountant so the loan database and the accounting records tie out.
* Own operational data quality and check that key fields match across closing records, servicing systems, administrator records and Finance systems; resolve any differences with the appropriate source owner.
* Maintain the master calendar for investor reporting, committee, board, audit, tax, compliance and portfolio deliverables and coordinate timely inputs from accountable content owners.

**Vendor Management and Process Improvement**

* Serve as the primary business owner for third-party fund administration, servicing, payment processing and related operational providers; set service standards, make sure the Foundation has access to the source records, and define how issues are escalated and when a provider can be replaced.
* Share vendor oversight with the Fund Accountant: this role owns the relationship, contract terms, service standards and timeliness; the Fund Accountant reviews the financial accuracy of what providers produce (interest, balances, investor statements and fund reports) before it is posted or shared.
* Monitor service performance, check that provider reports arrive on time and match the operating record (the Fund Accountant checks the financial figures) and lead resolution of errors, backlogs and control failures.
* Document and continuously improve workflows for approvals, closings, disbursements, servicing, amendments, reporting and record retention. Partner with the Fund Accountant where workflows touch the books, such as the monthly close; Finance owns accounting procedures and reconciliations.
* Design procedures that are durable, teachable and appropriately scaled rather than dependent on one employee's memory or heroics.

**Team Leadership and Coordination**

* Manage any future operations or servicing staff; establish clear ownership, service expectations and backup coverage.
* Run recurring operating meetings that convert cross-functional issues into decisions, named owners and deadlines.
* Refine roles, responsibilities, workflows, and accountability standards across teams involved in fund operations and investment management.
* Raise issues promptly and concisely with the Vice President, Impact Investing and enterprise leadership (legal and finance) when service failures, unresolved legal or financial questions, capacity constraints or control gaps threaten a closing, obligation or relationship.
* Build strong working relationships across teams while being willing to insist on complete documentation, clear authority and timely decisions.

**Qualifications**

**WHAT YOU BRING**

**Required**

* Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in fund operations, transaction management, loan administration, investment operations, structured finance, real estate finance, private credit, community development finance or a closely related field.
* Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business, real estate, public administration or a related field required.
* Demonstrated experience coordinating transactions through closing and funding, including legal documentation, cash mechanics and post-closing requirements.
* Working knowledge of financial statements, loan and investment documents, entity and fund records, payment and servicing processes, reconciliations and internal controls.
* Ability to build, lead, and evolve operational functions within a growing or complex organization.
* Confidence in evaluating existing practices, constructively challenging the status quo, and driving meaningful process improvements.
* Exceptional project management and organizational judgment, with the ability to maintain accuracy across multiple vehicles, transactions, deadlines and stakeholders.
* Strong written communication and the ability to convert complex requirements into clear checklists, procedures, records and short, clear updates for leadership when something is off track.
* Experience holding internal and external partners accountable, escalating appropriately and following issues through closure.
* A clear commitment to CFGA’s mission of equity and shared prosperity for all.

**Preferred**

* Experience with affordable housing, community development lending, program-related investments, impact investing or philanthropic investment vehicles.
* Experience managing a third-party fund administrator, loan servicer, closing counsel, tax provider or comparable outsourced operating partner.
* Experience building or improving an operating model, system of record, compliance calendar or reporting infrastructure.
* Comfort with Microsoft 365 tools such as SharePoint, Lists, Power Automate and Power BI; loan or relationship management systems such as Foundant or Salesforce; and tools used to summarize and check documents.
* Masters degree in relevant field.
* Relevant legal-operations, paralegal, fund-administration or project-management training is valuable; a law degree or CPA is not required.

**HYBRID SCHEDULE**

The Community Foundation operates in a hybrid working environment with staff working in-office three days per week and the opportunity to work two days remotely per week if in good standing.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
* Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.

**COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

Compensation will be determined based on experience and qualifications. The salary range is

$130,000 - $150,000. This position is exempt and eligible for the Foundation’s competitive health and benefits plan, which includes:

**Paid time off**

* Four weeks accrued paid vacation
* Two weeks accrued paid sick leave
* Four mental health days
* Two personal days
* Two floating holidays
* Ten holidays

**Benefits**

* All benefits effective on date of hire with no waiting period
* 100% employer-paid medical, dental and vision coverage for employee-only plans
* 100% employer-paid life insurance, AD&D, short-term disability and long-term disability
* 100% employer-paid downtown Atlanta parking or monthly MARTA card
* Affordable plans for legal insurance, critical illness, supplemental life and more
* Immediate eligibility to contribute to a 403(b), plus a 6% employer-paid contribution after one year regardless of employee contributions
* Cell phone stipend
* Employee Donor Advised Fund after one year
* Employee Assistance Program and more

**Culture, Learning & Development**

* Individual Development Plans with training, resources and development opportunities
* Two wellness rooms with self-care resources
* Monthly employee engagement activities

**TO APPLY**

Submit your resume and cover letter through our Careers website.

Note: Only applications submitted through our website will be accepted. Due to the volume of candidates, we are unable to provide status updates or accommodate phone calls or walk-ins regarding open positions.

The Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

KU Endowment is an independent, nonprofit organization and the official fundraising foundation for the University of Kansas. We partner with donors in providing philanthropic support to build a greater KU.

As an employee of KU Endowment, you’ll witness firsthand the power of our donors’ generosity. People are engaged. Purpose is ignited. Lives are changed.

**What we are looking for:**

The Senior Director/AVP, Fundraising Operations is the strategic operating leader responsible for translating advancement strategy into measurable fundraising performance. The role establishes the planning, analytics, management cadence, pipeline discipline, portfolio practices, and decision support that help fundraising leaders focus resources, improve execution, and achieve fundraising goals.

Serving as a trusted partner to executive leadership and frontline fundraising leaders, this role connects fundraising strategy, people, processes, data, and technology into a coherent revenue operating system. It provides visibility into performance, identifies risks and opportunities, and drives continuous improvement while enabling fundraisers and managers to spend more time building donor relationships and generating support.

The individual in this position is expected to embrace KU Endowment’s stated core values – collaboration, curiosity, empowerment, and excellence – and demonstrate support for them through professional interactions and activities.?

* Management experience required. Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and managing or developing analytical/operations teams preferred.

A Senior Director demonstrates the ability and experience necessary to lead and optimize KU Endowment’s Fundraising Operations function, translating strategy into execution through planning, analytics, technology, forecasting, and team leadership.

At our Support Center, we believe our best work is done Together, when departments collaborate and everyone is confident in contributing their ideas. This is why we are in the office 3 days per week.
  
  
Let’s Get Loco!
  
  
What’s in it for you!
  
  

* STRONG office culture recognized as a Great Place to Work® and driven by our core values: Simple. Together. Relentless. Ownership. Nimble. Growth
* Career growth opportunities
* Competitive pay and bonus potential
* Be an Owner: Equity Compensation
* Medical + Dental + Vision Insurance + HSA Savings Account
* 401(K) Retirement Plan with company match and immediate vesting
* Paid Vacation + Sick Pay + 12 Paid Holidays
* Employee Assistance Program
* Free El Pollo Loco food + restaurant discounts
* PerkSpot discounts program

**POSITION PURPOSE:**  
The Regional Director of Operations is responsible for driving El Pollo Loco’s success in the Los Angeles, CA region. They are responsible for providing operational expertise, strategic leadership and coaching. Directs, leads, manages and analyzes all aspects of the restaurant operations for the Areas under their direction to ensure achievement and maintenance of the regional sales, budgetary targets, controllable profit, performance metrics (e.g., service, quality, cleanliness, etc.), brand integrity, and compliance standards (e.g., food and restaurant safety, federal/state/local labor laws, etc.). Implements and executes strategic and tactical operational initiatives that support future business growth strategies. Oversees and manages adequate resource availability for existing and new restaurant openings including the attraction, retention, training, development and coaching of a high performing management team.
  
  
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**  

* Oversees all aspects of the region’s restaurant business, operations, and facilities. Directs and aligns company strategies with restaurant management activities.
* Utilizes reporting systems to determine trends in sales, cost of goods and guest services. Reviews, monitors and manages the financial progress of the individual restaurants and region, including food and labor costs, ensuring budgeted targets are achieved.
* Meets regularly with Area Leaders to coach, develop, train and review performance, share best practices and disseminate information on any areas where there is an opportunity for improvement (e.g., P&L, RCP, FSA, QSC, Mystery Shops, etc.). Develops action plans with Area Leaders to improve revenue, profitability and quality/service standards.
* Directs, manages and ensures the region’s successful and timely implementation of all marketing strategies and LTOs. Supports and inspects marketing strategies in building guest counts and sales.
* Provides effective and timely resolution to all guest and employee complaints, conflicts and employee relations that cannot be resolved at the Area Leader level.
* Ensures the region’s restaurants are in compliance with all local, regional, and national laws and have all the required documentation and paperwork.
* Leverages two-way communication with Field and Support Center employees. Represents the Operations perspective on prioritization, planning and promotions to inspire operational excellence, effective implementation and facilitate insights. Provides specific operational input and feedback into the development of new products and programs to ensure successful execution.
* Collaborates with Development, Human Resources, and Operations in the coordination and execution of new restaurant openings. Directs team selection, monitors the training and ensures the teams perform to El Pollo Loco’s standards. Participates in the local public relations support in all locations. Approves employee relocation within region ensuring moves are conducted in the most economical and efficient manner.
* Develops regional succession plans: evaluates open opportunities, assesses internal talent, oversees management training programs, and drives recruiting efforts to ensure adequate number of managers are available to sustain growth of the organization.
* Champions effective vertical and horizontal communications within the regional area including Company-wide news of interest, upcoming events, new facilities, promotions, product developments, “Best Practices” among peers, etc. Prepares thoroughly and delivers well-organized, dynamic and informative presentations to senior management as needed. Holds meetings with their respective teams on a regular basis to ensure fluid and consistent messaging.
* Creates and fosters a positive team environment through recognizing and reinforcing behaviors and results that are aligned with El Pollo Loco’s core values and culture. Ensures open channels for employee suggestions.
* Interacts professionally and ethically, constructively participating as a collaborative team leader in pursuit of common goals, including active attendance to meetings. Initiates cost-effective suggestions to improve operational procedures.
* Other activities, duties or responsibilities that are assigned by your supervisor.

QUALIFICATIONS – EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, LICENSE/CERTIFICATIONS:
  
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodation will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. The requirements listed below are representative of the education and/or experience required.
  
  
**Education/Work Experience:**  
High school diploma or equivalent (GED) required, BA/BS degree in Business Administration preferred. 8+ years QSR/multi-site restaurant experience as an Area Leader or District Manager required; 5+ years regional QSR management experience preferred; 3+ years El Pollo Loco experience preferred; and a track record of success in leading, managing, coaching and developing high performance teams.
  
  
**License/Certifications:**  
Current valid driver’s license required as frequent weekly travel is involved. Current ServSafe certification preferred.
  
  
**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:**  

* Experience with successfully recruiting, building, and developing a team (based on current and future needs).
* Confidence in execution of strategic initiatives.
* Must be decisive and able to make fact-based decisions.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving mindset and skills; meticulous attention to detail
* Ability to effectively communicate with internal and external business partners.
* Ability to prioritize and plan work assignments and work under pressure of frequent and tight deadlines.
* Ability to read, write, and interpret complex reports, documents, and correspondence.
* Adept at managing and prioritizing competing time sensitive requests while working well in a team atmosphere that may be under pressure.
* Ability to exercise independent judgment on matters of significance to the company.
* Ability to work weekends and extended work schedules as needed.
* Must be willing and able to travel locally within Southern California and to out-of-state restaurant locations, as needed by car or airplane.

Our Company
  
  
In 1980 the first American El Pollo Loco opened on Alvarado Street in Los Angeles, quickly becoming a destination for the best citrus-marinated, fire-grilled pollo in town. Over the past four decades, El Pollo Loco has grown into more than 500 restaurants across 9 states, becoming an L.A. mainstay and cultural benchmark along the way. And today, we continue to work just as hard to always provide customers with fresh and innovative L.A. Mex from our famous family dinners to Mexican entrees.
  
  
The pay range identified is the hourly or salary rate El Pollo Loco expects to pay for the posted position. This range does not include any benefits or bonus opportunities that might be available for the position based on position and eligibility criteria. Individual pay will vary based on a variety of factors including years of experience, industry experience, education, geography, etc.

**Job Description**
-------------------

The Opportunity
  
  
The St. Jude Leadership Academy is building the systems, experiences and capabilities that help leaders across St. Jude grow their impact. We’re looking for a Director of Academy Operations who can help turn that vision into an enterprise-scale reality.

This is a role for a builder.

  
  

As the Academy’s primary operational leader and integrator, you’ll translate strategy into an integrated portfolio of work and create the infrastructure needed to move ideas from concept through implementation, evaluation and scale. You’ll work across Leadership Development, Culture Strategy and institutional partners to connect priorities, clarify ownership and turn complex, cross-functional work into coordinated action.

  
  

You’ll also serve as a strategic thought partner to senior leadership, bringing visibility to priorities, tradeoffs, resources and execution risks while helping shape how the Academy delivers its work across St. Jude.

  
  

Because the Leadership Academy operates as a small, highly collaborative team, this isn’t a role where strategy gets handed off once the plan is built. You’ll move comfortably between enterprise-level thinking and hands-on execution, building the systems that allow a small team to have an outsized impact across St. Jude.

  
  

### **What You’ll Do**

  
  

As Director of Academy Operations, you will:

  
  

* **Turn strategy into execution.** Translate Leadership Academy priorities into an integrated portfolio, implementation roadmap and operating plan.
* **Lead complex work from idea to impact.** Guide cross-functional initiatives from concept and design through implementation, evaluation and scale.
* **Build the Academy’s operating infrastructure.** Establish governance, decision points, roles, handoffs, planning processes and operating rhythms that create clarity and accountability.
* **Connect work across St. Jude.** Build strong partnerships across Leadership Development, Culture Strategy and other institutional functions, bringing people and priorities together while maintaining clear roles and ownership.
* **See around corners.** Identify dependencies, duplication, capacity constraints, gaps and execution risks across the Academy’s portfolio and drive solutions.
* **Create visibility into impact.** Establish portfolio-level measures, dashboards and reporting that show progress, outcomes and organizational impact.
* **Help good ideas scale.** Develop practical approaches for moving promising concepts and pilots into sustainable institutional practices.
* **Lead operational and resource planning.** Oversee budgets, resources, technology, vendors, contracts and external partnerships that support the Academy’s work.
* **Drive continuous improvement.** Apply human-centered design, agile and continuous-improvement approaches to strengthen programs, processes and operations.
* **Serve as a strategic advisor.** Help senior leadership navigate priorities, tradeoffs, sequencing, resource allocation and execution risk.
* **Communicate with influence.** Develop executive-level materials and clearly communicate progress, decisions, risks and recommendations to senior stakeholders.
* **Stay close to the work.** Remain directly involved in execution when needed, reflecting the hands-on, highly collaborative nature of the Academy team.
* **Develop people and teams.** Create clarity around goals and expectations while supporting performance, engagement, professional growth and meaningful career experiences.
  

  

**What You Bring**
------------------

  
  

You are an experienced operations and program leader who knows how to take an ambitious vision and build the structure required to make it real. You are comfortable navigating complexity, influencing across organizational boundaries and leading work when accountability is shared across multiple teams.

  
  

You bring:

  
  

* A bachelor’s degree; an advanced degree is preferred.
* 10+ years of related professional experience.
* Significant experience leading complex enterprise programs, operations, transformation initiatives or similar work within a large organization.
* Demonstrated experience building operating models, processes or organizational capabilities, not simply administering established programs.
* A track record of translating strategic objectives into operational plans and driving those plans through execution.
* Demonstrated success leading complex, cross-functional work in environments where accountability and authority are distributed.
* Strong strategic program management, operational, analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
* The ability to move comfortably between enterprise-level strategy and detailed execution.
* Strong consulting, stakeholder-management and influencing skills, including experience partnering with senior leaders.
* Experience with budget planning, resource management, vendor relationships and contract negotiations.
* Experience with human-centered design, agile methods, continuous improvement or related approaches.
* Strong written, verbal and executive communication skills.
* Experience in leadership development, organizational development, talent, culture or another people-related function is preferred, but not required.
  

  

**The Kind of Leader Who Will Thrive Here**
-------------------------------------------

  
  

This role may be especially compelling if you:

  
  

* See complexity and instinctively begin creating clarity and structure.
* Get energy from building something, not simply maintaining what already exists.
* Can zoom out to see the enterprise picture and then zoom back in to make sure the details work.
* Know how to lead through influence when the people needed to accomplish the work don’t necessarily report to you.
* Are comfortable asking difficult questions about priorities, capacity, tradeoffs and risk.
* Enjoy turning promising ideas into repeatable, sustainable ways of working.
* Believe measurement should help people make better decisions, not simply create more reporting.
* Approach problems with curiosity and are willing to challenge established ways of working when there is a better path forward.
* Can advise senior leaders one moment and roll up your sleeves to solve an execution problem the next.
* Want to build systems that make it possible for other people to do exceptional work.
  

  
  

**Key Capabilities**
--------------------

  
  

Enterprise program leadership • Operational strategy • Portfolio management • Cross-functional integration • Systems thinking • Execution • Consultative problem solving • Stakeholder influence • Human-centered problem solving • Measurement and analytics • Continuous improvement • Organizational change

  
  

**Why St. Jude**
----------------

  
  

At St. Jude, operational excellence ultimately serves a larger purpose. The work of the Leadership Academy helps equip leaders across the institution to lead people, navigate change and advance a mission unlike any other.

  
  

As Director of Academy Operations, you’ll have the opportunity to help shape not only what the Leadership Academy delivers, but how it works: building the infrastructure, partnerships and operating practices that allow a small team to create meaningful impact across St. Jude.

  
  

**Minimum Education and/or Training:**

  
  

* Bachelor's degree required.
* Master's degree preferred.
  

  

**Minimum Experience:**

  
  

* 10+ years related experience.
* Significant experience managing large teams and building systems and processes to improve efficiency and effectiveness.
* Experience translating strategic goals into operational goals and overseeing execution.
* Proven experience leading administration & operations management, driving execution, managing stakeholders, budget planning & resource mgmt.
* Prior experience in vendor contract negotiations and strategic vendor relationship management.
* Proven performance in earlier role/comparable role.
  

  
  

This position is remote within approved U.S. locations. Due to state-specific employment regulations, we are unable to consider applicants currently residing in California for remote work; however, candidates based in California who are willing to relocate to an approved location may be considered.

**Compensation**

In recognition of certain U.S. state and municipal pay transparency laws, St. Jude is including a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This is an estimate offered in good faith and a specific salary offer takes into account factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the salary range and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current salary range is $125,840 - $238,160 per year for the role of Director, Academy Operations.

Explore our exceptional benefits!

  
  

We are committed to a human-centered hiring experience. Technology may support portions of our process, but recruiting decisions involve human review and engagement. Learn more about our approach to AI.

  
  

St. Jude is an Equal Opportunity Employer

  
  

**No Search Firms**

St. Jude Children's Research Hospital does not accept unsolicited assistance from search firms for employment opportunities. Please do not call or email. All resumes submitted by search firms to any employee or other representative at St. Jude via email, the internet or in any form and/or method without a valid written search agreement in place and approved by HR will result in no fee being paid in the event the candidate is hired by St. Jude.

Restaurant Depot is the nation’s leading members-only, wholesale cash-and-carry supplier serving independent restaurants, caterers, delis, convenience stores, & other foodservice businesses across 165+ locations in 35 states. Our stores offer bulk quantities of fresh meat, seafood, produce, dairy, frozen foods, grocery items, beverages, paper goods, cleaning supplies, restaurant equipment, & more. Open seven days a week, we are committed to delivering quality products, competitive pricing, & exceptional service to our members. As we continue to grow, we are seeking an experienced Director of Operations to provide strategic leadership, drive operational performance, & support the continued success of our store network.

**Position Summary**

The Director of Operations provides strategic leadership & operational oversight for a multi-region portfolio of stores. This role is responsible for driving business performance through operational excellence, financial accountability, talent development, customer experience, regulatory compliance, & growth initiatives. The Director partners closely with executive leadership to develop & execute company strategies while leading Regional Managers & field leadership teams in achieving organizational goals.

This position plays a key role in establishing operational standards, improving profitability, developing future leaders, & ensuring consistent execution across all locations. Responsibilities include oversight of P&L performance, labor management, sales growth, food safety, regulatory compliance, customer satisfaction, workforce planning, & organizational development.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership & Business Performance**

* Develop & execute operational strategies that support company growth, sales performance, & profitability objectives.
* Lead Regional Managers & field leadership teams through clear performance expectations, accountability measures, & ongoing performance reviews.
* Analyze sales, labor, margin, shrink, inventory, & operational metrics to identify opportunities & implement corrective actions.
* Drive sustainable sales growth, market share expansion, & EBITDA improvement across assigned regions.
* Partner with executive leadership on long-term business planning, budgets, capital investments, & new store development opportunities.
* Ensure operational priorities align with company objectives & strategic initiatives.

**Financial Management & Operational Excellence**

* Maintain accountability for P&L performance across assigned regions & divisions.
* Develop annual operating plans, labor strategies, budgets, & financial forecasts.
* Monitor key performance indicators, including sales growth, gross margin, labor productivity, inventory turns, EBITDA, shrink, & waste.
* Establish & maintain consistent operational standards across all locations.
* Ensure effective execution of company programs, policies, procedures, & initiatives.
* Lead continuous improvement efforts focused on productivity, efficiency, process optimization, & customer experience.
* Drive accountability for operational audits, food safety standards, inventory accuracy, & facility maintenance.
* Implement best practices to improve profitability & overall operating efficiency.

**Customer Experience & Brand Standards**

* Champion a customer-first culture throughout the organization.
* Ensure stores consistently deliver exceptional customer service & maintain company brand standards.
* Review customer feedback & satisfaction trends, developing action plans to address opportunities for improvement.
* Lead initiatives that strengthen customer loyalty, retention, & overall brand reputation.

**Talent Development & Workforce Management**

* Build a strong leadership pipeline through succession planning, talent development, & career progression opportunities.
* Coach & develop Regional Managers, District Managers, Store Managers, & emerging leaders.
* Establish leadership development programs & promote internal growth opportunities.
* Lead performance management processes & reinforce organizational accountability.
* Develop workforce & labor strategies that maximize productivity while supporting operational needs.
* Ensure staffing models, recruitment, & retention initiatives align with current & future business requirements.
* Oversee labor budgets, staffing levels, & productivity targets across assigned regions.
* Foster a culture of engagement, collaboration, accountability, & continuous improvement.

**Compliance, Risk Management & Food Safety**

* Ensure compliance with company policies & applicable federal, state, & local regulations.
* Maintain accountability for food safety, HACCP, OSHA, labor law compliance, & health department standards.
* Partner with Human Resources & Legal teams on employee relations matters, investigations, & risk mitigation.
* Lead operational audits & corrective action programs to address compliance & performance gaps.
* Ensure all locations meet company standards for workplace safety, security, & regulatory compliance.

**Change Management & Strategic Initiatives**

* Lead companywide operational initiatives, process improvements, & transformational projects.
* Support acquisitions, store integrations, remodels, & new store openings.
* Drive adoption of new technologies, operating procedures, & business processes.
* Collaborate with executive leadership on strategic growth initiatives & organizational priorities.

**Communication & Executive Partnership**

* Serve as a key operational liaison between field leadership & executive management.
* Provide executive reporting on operational performance, business trends, risks, & opportunities.
* Facilitate regular business reviews with Regional Managers & key stakeholders.
* Communicate company vision, priorities, & performance expectations throughout the organization.
* Partner with cross-functional departments to improve operational alignment & execution.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, Retail Management, or a related field required; MBA preferred.
* 10–15 years of progressive multi-unit operations leadership experience.
* Minimum 5 years of experience leading Regional Managers, District Managers, or equivalent senior field leadership teams.
* Demonstrated success managing large-scale, high-volume, multi-location operations.
* Proven track record of driving sales growth, profitability improvement, & operational excellence.
* Strong background in P&L management, labor management, financial analysis, budgeting, & strategic planning.
* Experience leading organizational change, business transformation, & large-scale operational initiatives.
* Extensive knowledge of regulatory compliance, food safety, labor laws, & risk management.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, coaching, & team development skills.
* Advanced analytical, decision-making, & problem-solving abilities.
* Ability to travel extensively throughout assigned regions.

**Compensation & Benefits**

* Competitive salary commensurate with experience
* Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance Coverage
* 401(k) Retirement Plan with Employer Match
* Paid Time Off (PTO) in accordance with company policy
* Six (6) Paid Company Holidays
* Tuition Reimbursement Program, subject to eligibility & plan guidelines
* Additional Voluntary Supplemental Benefits, which may include life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance programs, & other optional benefits
* Competitive & Comprehensive Benefits Package Designed to Support You & Your Family

Job Summary - Why you’ll love this position

Are you motivated by the challenge of solving complex, enterprise-wide problems? Do you love asking "why" and transforming good operations into exceptional public experiences? If so, consider joining the State of Missouri as our next Director of Operational Excellence!

In this pivotal leadership role you will champion continuous improvement across state government, lead our operational initiatives, and oversee our statewide customer experience program. This position resides within the Office of Administration, the administrative arm of the executive branch, but leads efforts that span all executive agencies to improve service delivery to the citizens of Missouri.

We are seeking an energetic, visionary executive to lead and empower a dedicated team of process improvement and customer experience efforts while serving as a strategic partner to executive leadership, agency partners, and frontline public servants. Our next director is a bridge-builder who combines proven improvement methodologies with human-centered design, modern customer experience principles, rapid responsiveness to agency partner needs, and a passion for coaching state team members to achieve measurable public outcomes.

In addition to the inspiring work that will improve the services provided by state government and your colleagues work environment, you will receive a great benefits package that includes paid time off, medical/vision/dental insurance, life insurance, and retirement.

*The salary indicated represents a base pay rate. If the individual selected or the position is eligible for a pay differential (e.g., shift, security, or years of service), it will be added to the total compensation in your paycheck. A pay differential does not raise your base pay.*

Responsibilities - What you’ll do

* Work collaboratively with leadership and teams to encourage, develop, and execute strategies to create a culture of continuous improvement across Missouri state government. Measure the effectiveness of improvements and provide administration with visibility to such improvements.
* Act as a subject matter expert and promote change management by sharing Lean Six Sigma and other Operational Excellence best practices. Teach, mentor, coach and lead Operational Excellence leaders from every state department.
* Continuously provide helpful operational excellence resources for team members and facilitate training sessions.
* Model excellence in leadership and act with urgency to achieve results and lead efforts to cultivate a culture of data-based decision making.
* Facilitate, lead, and oversee state level strategic initiatives and other projects as assigned by leadership.
* Coordinate and host an annual Show Me Excellence Summit and represent the State of Missouri at national operational excellence events.

Qualifications - All you need for success

**Minimum Qualifications**

* A bachelor’s degree or equivalent
* Formal training in Lean Six Sigma or an equivalent continuous process improvement framework. Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification is strongly preferred
* Demonstrated advanced knowledge in Lean and Operational Excellence frameworks and facilitation methodologies
* Hands-on experience work with survey, feedback, or data visualization platforms, such as Qualtrics, Tableau, or Power BI

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Must be action oriented, demonstrate superior organizational abilities and have strong facilitation skills and excellent communications skills.
* Ability to work with leaders and multi-level teams to establish goals, performance indicators, actions plans and deliverables and effectively communicating across broad audiences.
* Must have excellent leadership abilities. This individual must be an effective collaborator with energy, enthusiasm and a can-do attitude who can empower others, gain buy-in and achieve results.
* Good understanding of data analysis related to process improvement and an ability to analyze data to gain insights and support problem solving.
* Training, certification, and/or education in continuous process improvement programs such as Lean Six Sigma as well as completion of Missouri Way, Leadership Academy, and similar programs is preferred.

***Lack of post******‐******secondary education will not be used as the sole basis denying consideration to any applicant.***

Successful background check results are required for employment in this position. This may include background checks involving a candidate's name and/or fingerprints and other screenings as needed for the specific position.

Authorization to work in the United States is a prerequisite of employment. The Office of Administration will not sponsor applicants for work visas.

Job Details - More reasons to love this position

The State of Missouri offers an excellent benefits package that includes a defined pension plan, generous amounts of leave and holiday time, and eligibility for health insurance coverage. Your total compensation is more than the dollars you receive in your paycheck. To help demonstrate the value of working for the State of Missouri, we have created an interactive Total Compensation Calculator. This tool provides a comprehensive view of benefits and more that are offered to prospective employees. The Total Compensation Calculator and other applicant resources can be found here.

OARecruiters@oa.mo.gov

They advance our mission and exemplify excellence, compassion, teamwork and purpose in all that they do****.*** Indiana University Health is seeking individuals who embody these values to join our System Services leadership team in the role of Executive Director, System Operational Excellence.

The **Executive Director, System Operational Excellence** provides enterprise leadership for IU Health’s operational excellence strategy, management system, and continuous improvement efforts. This highly visible leader will partner with executive and operational leaders across the organization to advance performance improvement initiatives that strengthen quality, safety, workforce engagement, service, and operational outcomes. Leading a high-performing team, the Executive Director will play a key role in aligning improvement efforts with organizational priorities and driving measurable, system-wide impact.

This leader will be responsible for advancing and maturing IU Health’s Lean management system, developing leaders’ problem-solving capabilities, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement across a complex, matrixed healthcare environment. This is a unique opportunity to build upon a strong operational excellence foundation and help shape the future of performance improvement at IU Health by developing leaders, strengthening organizational capabilities, and accelerating strategic priorities across the enterprise.

**Key Relationships**

Reports to: Vice President – Operational Excellence

**Candidate Qualifications**

Candidates for the position will be evaluated according to the following criteria and competencies.

* Bachelor's Degree is required. Master's Degree is preferred.
* Requires 10 plus years of relevant experience.
* Requires 4 years of people leader experience.
* Requires a minimum of 5 years of experience within a complex healthcare system.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification is required. Master Black Belt is preferred.
* Must have a demonstrated record of sustaining improvements after implementation.
* Requires experience developing and delivering Lean/DMAIC training programs.
* Requires experience helping establish Operational Excellence strategy, priorities, and multi-year roadmaps.
* Requires a proven ability to influence leaders in a large matrixed organization.

* Requires the ability to facilitate large groups and drive consensus among stakeholders.
* Requires the ability to teach improvement methodology from frontline staff through executive leadership.
* Requires strong coaching, mentoring, and adult learning skills.
* Requires portfolio management and project prioritization expertise.
* Requires the ability to connect improvement work directly to organizational strategy and performance outcomes.
* Additional Lean certification (Shingo, LEI, AME, etc.) is preferred.

records.title: Head of Plant Production Engineering
records.description:
Your Contribution
=================

The Head of Plant Production Engineering is responsible for leading all Production Engineering activities associated with customer projects, product acquisitions, new product launches, industrialization, and production readiness within the plant. This position serves as the plant's primary owner for Production Engineering processes, ensuring successful execution of the Product Development Process (PDP) from acquisition through Start of Production (SOP) and ramp-up. The role provides leadership to Production Engineers, drives standardization and deployment of manufacturing concepts, ensures manufacturability of product designs, manages capital investments, and represents Operations within project core teams. The Plant Head of Production Engineering ensures project launches meet safety, quality, delivery, cost, and operational performance objectives.

* Lead, develop, coach, & manage the plant Production Engineering organization.
* Build organizational capability to support current and future product launches.
* Own industrialization activities for all customer projects within the plant. Ensure successful execution of product launches from acquisition and business transfer through SOP and stabilization.
* Lead development of manufacturing concepts, production processes, line layouts, and assembly strategies.
* Ensure product designs are manufacturable and meet operational standards.
* Coordinate launch readiness across Manufacturing Engineering, Tooling Engineering, Quality, Logistics, Purchasing, and Operations Support acquisition reviews and participate in PAC, PRC, and pre-development activities.
* Ensure implementation of Design-for-Manufacturing principles throughout project development. Ensure compliance with MAHLE PDP milestones, gates, deliverables, and timing requirements. Oversee completion of all Production Engineering deliverables throughout all quality gates.
* Monitor project status, risks, cost performance, capacity requirements, and launch readiness. Lead escalation activities when project risks threaten timing, quality, or cost objectives. Review project dashboards and launch metrics with plant leadership and program teams.
* Approve and govern: Manufacturing concepts, Process flows, Plant layouts, Assembly concepts, Material flow strategies, Value stream integration.
* Ensure application of Lean Manufacturing and Manufacturing Optimization Process (MOP) methodologies in alignment with Operations Excellence Manager.
* Drive takt-time analysis, line balancing, ergonomic studies, and capacity planning. Validate cycle times using MTM or equivalent engineering methods. Ensure implementation of standardized manufacturing processes across the region.
* Ensure development, completion, and approval of Process FMEA (P-FMEA), Control Plans, Special Characteristics, Process Capability Studies, Validation Plans. Support flawless launch activities and manufacturing risk reduction. Lead readiness reviews for installation checks, internal process approval, internal run at rate, customer run at rate, PPAP readiness. Ensure production systems consistently achieve quality and operational KPI’s.
* Lead capital expenditure planning and approval activities. Validate business cases and investment requirements. Ensure optimal utilization of existing equipment before requesting new capital. Support supplier selection through PDC and SDC processes. Approve manufacturing equipment specifications. Participate in procurement and acceptance of production equipment, tooling, fixtures, and test systems.
* Chair Production Engineering project meetings, and lead the plant Production Engineering Extended Team, ensuring effective communication between Project Core Teams and Plant Extended Teams.

Your Experience & Qualifications

* Bachelor’s Degree required, B.S. in Engineering, or related technical discipline required. Master’s Degree preferred.
* 8+ years’ experience in manufacturing, launch, industrialization, or production engineering.
* 5+ years’ progressive leadership responsibility regarding engineering or manufacturing operations.
* Demonstrated success in leading complex product launches and PDP projects.
* Experience in an automotive manufacturing facility required; high volume, medium to large campus experience preferred.
* Demonstrated knowledge in IATF16949, ISO14001 and 45001 Audits and processes.
* Excellent diagnostic abilities / root cause analysis required; Lean Six Sigma and Black Belt certification strongly preferred.

We will provide a collaborative environment working on exciting assignments, along with ongoing personal & career development opportunities.
